proposals.approach_summary:
Stance: a roughly 200-line in-house agent loop on an additively extended ChatModel port. No agent framework. LangGraph is removed (its two linear graphs become plain functions). Paths are relative to C:/Users/Nima/Desktop/MINE/My_projects/Dutch Learning Platform/Final_Project_v1.

P5, in order: LlmGateway (one reserve/call/settle path, one failure policy, agent_runs audit) under every existing call site; ChatModel v2 (respond() and stream() beside untouched complete/complete_once, strict schemas, scripted fixture, Ollama tools); a hand-written httpx Azure adapter on the stateless Responses API; runtime, tool registry and SQL learner snapshot; GenAI spans plus an eval harness reusing production prompts and validators; the Data Zone Standard model migration with a retirement check; SSE through the Next proxy.

P6: tutor (authored explanation first, model for why-follow-ups, grounded quotes, deterministic mini-drill, remembered error categories); study guide (model picks and orders candidate ids and reason codes, code writes the reasons, daily cache, planner fallback); partner (interpret, code validates, generated reaction plus authored anchor behind a contradiction guard, cited feedback, validated generated scenarios in a review queue).

Real weaknesses of the stance: we own Responses wire-format drift and hand-rolled telemetry conventions; no ready-made memory, checkpointing or MCP; thread-per-stream concurrency; single-maintainer knowledge; weak tool calling on llama3.1:8b locally.

Critical files (under that root): apps/api/src/dlp/providers/base.py; apps/api/src/dlp/providers/chat_openai_compatible.py; apps/api/src/dlp/domains/usage/service.py; apps/api/src/dlp/domains/topic_conversations/service.py; apps/web/app/api/[...path]/route.ts.

key_decisions.choice: In-house loop in apps/api/src/dlp/domains/agents/runtime.py built directly on the ChatModel port; no Microsoft Agent Framework, no LangGraph agents, no Foundry agents.
key_decisions.why: (1) The product's invariants are the hard part: reserve-before-call, at-most-once, one HTTP request per step (pinned for 14 failure kinds in tests/test_single_model_call.py), body-free logs, substring grounding. Today they are asserted against httpx.MockTransport; a framework chat client owns retries, streaming and telemetry, so each invariant becomes middleware against framework internals that must be re-verified on every upgrade. (2) ENGINEERING.md forbids domain code depending on vendor SDKs; framework Agent/tool/session types would leak into domains or be wrapped so thinly the framework adds nothing. (3) Scope is three agents, at most 4 steps and about 6 tools each, one replica, a fully synchronous stack; Agent Framework's Python API is async-first and would need an event-loop bridge into sync SQLAlchemy code. (4) CI and e2e must run on a scripted fixture and local dev on Ollama; a fixture ChatModel is needed either way. (5) Microsoft's own guidance says to write a function when a function will do, and Foundry Agent Service does not support strict structured outputs (confirmed in the Azure structured-outputs doc). (6) Reversible: Tool(args model, handler) and AgentSpec map 1:1 onto framework function tools; only the loop would be thrown away.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Agent Framework 1.0 in-process (extra dependency tree incl. openai SDK, async bridge, its OTel emits what it chooses, fixture parity still ours). LangGraph create_react_agent/ToolNode (langchain-core message types and langsmith in the image, checkpointing we do not use because state already lives in PostgreSQL rows). Foundry hosted agents (excluded by the owner; second state store; no strict outputs). The honest cost of this choice is listed in open_risks.

key_decisions.choice: Remove. practice/workflow.py and topic_conversations/workflow.py become three plain functions called in sequence; build_graph(chat).invoke(state) survives as a tiny pipeline object so tests/test_turns.py patches keep working. Drop langgraph from pyproject.toml and regenerate requirements-azure.lock.
key_decisions.why: Both graphs are START→a→b→c→END, compiled on every call, with no conditional edge, ToolNode or checkpointer. The dependency pulls langgraph, langgraph-checkpoint, langgraph-prebuilt, langgraph-sdk, langchain-core, langchain-protocol and langsmith into a hash-pinned production image for zero runtime behaviour.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Keep it for the linear graphs (two orchestration styles side by side, recursion_limit=6 silently capping future loops); grow it into the agent runtime (see decision above).

key_decisions.choice: Additive only in providers/base.py: Role gains 'tool'; ChatMessage gains tool_calls, tool_call_id, opaque (defaults); new ToolCall, ToolSpec(name, description, parameters: type[BaseModel]), ChatStreamEvent (TextDelta | ToolCallDelta | Completed(result)); ChatResult gains tool_calls, finish_reason, reasoning_tokens, cached_tokens, billed_input_tokens, billed_output_tokens appended after raw; two new NON-abstract methods respond(messages, *, tools=(), tool_choice='auto', schema=None, max_output_tokens=400, temperature=0.2, reasoning_effort='none', timeout_seconds=None, prompt_version='v0', request_id='') and stream(same). respond() is exactly one request. Default respond() without tools delegates to self.complete_once; with tools it raises ProviderUnavailable(sent=False). Default stream() yields one delta from respond().
key_decisions.why: complete/complete_once signatures and semantics stay byte-identical, so the positional ChatResult constructions, the Mock assert_called_once_with in test_single_model_call.py, the (messages, **kwargs) monkeypatches and the benchmark models in benchmarks/language/harness.py keep working without edits. Delegating the tool-less default to complete_once means existing monkeypatches still intercept.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Adding tools/stream kwargs to complete (breaks the pinned call assertions and every subclass signature); a second port class (two registries, two fixtures).

key_decisions.choice: New providers/chat_azure_responses.py (AzureResponsesChatModel) using hand-written httpx against POST {endpoint}/openai/v1/responses with store:false, input items rebuilt from our messages each step, max_output_tokens, reasoning.effort, text.format {type:json_schema,name,schema,strict:true}, tools [{type:function,name,description,parameters,strict:true}], parallel_tool_calls:false, stream:true for stream(). Encrypted reasoning items returned in output are echoed back via ChatMessage.opaque between tool steps. OpenAICompatibleChatModel stays for Ollama and as AZURE_CHAT_API=chat_completions rollback (gpt-4.1-mini only).
key_decisions.why: Verified in Microsoft docs (Sept 2026): Responses is GA in westeurope; gpt-5.6 models cannot combine reasoning with function tools on Chat Completions ('use /v1/responses'); reasoning models reject temperature and max_tokens; strict outputs require parallel_tool_calls false; stateless mode returns encrypted reasoning items by default. Stateless keeps PostgreSQL the only copy of learner text (store:true keeps it at Azure for 30 days). httpx keeps transport injection for the one-request tests, no SDK retries (openai SDK defaults to 2), no SDK debug logging of bodies, and no new hashed dependencies.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: openai SDK inside the adapter (allowed by the rule, but hidden retries and a larger lock file; revisit if the wire format churns); previous_response_id/Conversations API (second state store); staying on Chat Completions (blocks tools on current models).

key_decisions.decision: Reasoning effort, temperature and token ceilings
key_decisions.choice: Port default reasoning_effort='none'. Interpretation, ranking, translation and partner reaction use 'none'; tutor, study guide, feedback, scenario and story writing use 'low'. The Azure adapter never sends temperature unless AZURE_CHAT_SEND_TEMPERATURE=true. max_output_tokens is treated as the total cap including reasoning tokens.
key_decisions.why: With effort none the existing ceilings (400/600/1600) keep their meaning; the docs state max_output_tokens covers reasoning plus visible output. Determinism formerly bought with temperature 0.0 is replaced by strict schemas plus code validators and measured by the eval suites before cutover.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Default 'medium' (model default; would truncate 400-token interpretation calls and triple cost); keeping temperature (HTTP 400 on every current West Europe model).

key_decisions.choice: DataZoneStandard (EU) in West Europe. chat-small = gpt-5.6-luna 2026-07-09, chat-strong = gpt-5.6-terra 2026-07-09 (both GA, retire 2028-01-11). Quota fallback: gpt-5.4-mini 2026-03-17 / gpt-5.4. gpt-6-luna is a later, eval-gated parameter change. versionUpgradeOption stays NoAutoUpgrade, guarded by scripts/check_model_lifecycle.py.
key_decisions.why: Verified: regional Standard in westeurope offers only gpt-4.1-mini (Deprecated, retires 2027-04-14); the listed models are available there under Data Zone Standard; GO_LIVE already says not to pick Global silently. An automatic upgrade would swap the model without passing the eval gate. The ARM Models API exposes lifecycleStatus and deprecation.inference for the check.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: GlobalStandard (cheaper, data leaves the EU zone); OnceCurrentVersionExpired (unvetted model in production); staying on gpt-4.1-mini (hard stop in six months, no tools+reasoning path).

key_decisions.choice: Legacy single-call sites: gateway.call()/reserve()/settle() inside the caller's transaction with the caller's existing estimate (behaviour and pinned numbers unchanged). Agent runs: begin_run() reserves the WHOLE run budget (model_calls=max_steps, tokens=max_total_tokens) and inserts agent_runs(status=running) in its own committed transaction; provider calls run with no transaction open; finish_run() does feature writes + usage settle + audit in one transaction. At-most-once = unique(learner_id, agent, request_id) plus a partial unique index on (learner_id, agent) where status='running'; a stale running row is marked interrupted and charged in full, never replayed.
key_decisions.why: Satisfies 'reserved before it runs' for every step with one reservation, removes row locks and usage_counters locks from agent model calls, and survives crashes without silent replay. The loop enforces remaining = reserved − used before every step.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Per-step reservations (N lock round trips, partial-failure settlement complexity); holding paid_model_guard advisory lock across a multi-call run (blocks every other paid role for the whole run, is transaction-scoped anyway).

key_decisions.choice: Nothing was sent (usage refusal, paid gate, ProviderUnavailable with sent=False from httpx.ConnectError, exception before the first provider call) → release. A request may have reached the provider (timeout, 5xx, malformed, validation failure, mid-stream abort) → commit max(measured, estimate). Success → commit billed tokens across all attempts and attempts as model calls.
key_decisions.why: Replaces three inconsistent behaviours across about 11 sites and fixes two known flaws: connection-refused being charged in full at commit-estimate sites, and repair attempts being billed but not counted.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Per-site policies (status quo); always release on failure (under-counts paid work, contradicts LEARNING_AGENTS 'conservative usage is retained').

key_decisions.decision: Tools: what the model may touch
key_decisions.choice: Eager compact context (snapshot summary, subject facts) plus lazy READ tools that wrap existing functions inside SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY, with learner_id injected from ToolContext and args models that have extra='forbid' and no learner field. PROPOSE tools never write: they validate and stash a normalized proposal in run scratch and return {accepted, errors:[codes]}; code applies accepted proposals in finish_run. The final structured output is itself a proposal validated by AgentSpec.validate with one repair turn.
key_decisions.why: Keeps 'models propose, code decides' literal, makes cross-learner access structurally impossible, and keeps most runs at 1–2 model calls. stories.service.today_episode and stories.service.library are deliberately NOT tools because they lock/insert StorySeries and can enqueue a paid job.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Generic SQL/query tool; write tools with post-hoc audit; tool-only design with no eager context (more steps, more tokens).

key_decisions.decision: Streaming transport and what may be streamed
key_decisions.choice: SSE over POST fetch (not EventSource) on the same routes via Accept: text/event-stream; sync def route does all pre-stream checks then returns StreamingResponse over a sync generator that owns its own session_scope() transactions. Events: run, status, delta, result, error, done, each with an incrementing id. Only advisory tutor prose (explanation.nl, placed first in the schema because strict outputs keep schema key order) is token-streamed, shown as 'wordt gecontroleerd'; correct_form, quotes, drill and every partner reply are sent only after validation (client typewriter). Replay of a finished request_id returns one result event; there is no mid-stream resume.
key_decisions.why: EventSource cannot POST or set X-Requested-With. The whole stack is sync, so a threadpool generator avoids a parallel async provider client; one thread per live stream is fine for one learner. Showing unvalidated partner lines or answer keys would break 'code keeps validating everything'.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: async route + AsyncClient (duplicate adapter code paths); WebSocket (Next route handlers cannot upgrade); streaming everything (unvalidated content on screen); resumable streams with an event buffer (not worth it for 3–6 s replies on one replica).

key_decisions.choice: Free first: when the subject already has an explanation (authored question explanation from topics.save_topic_practice, the stored writing correction explanation, a feedback point note) the first tutor message is that text with no model call. The model runs for why-follow-ups (cap 3 per thread), for subjects without an authored explanation, and to choose category/drill. One thread per (learner, subject_hash) is the cache.
key_decisions.why: Most 'Leg uit' taps cost nothing and always have a deterministic fallback; the agent adds value exactly where the owner asked (why-follow-ups, drill, memory).
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Always generate (cost and latency for text we already hold); cross-learner explanation cache (one learner today).

key_decisions.decision: Study guide: who writes the reasons
key_decisions.choice: Model selects 3–5 activity ids from code-built candidates, orders them, assigns a reason_code from an enum and writes one focus sentence. Code pins mandatory steps (due words ≥5, ready episode), checks each reason_code against snapshot facts, and renders the trilingual reason from templates with SQL numbers. The focus sentence must pass a deny-list (level, weakness, mastery, pronunciation) and may only contain digits present in the snapshot.
key_decisions.why: Gives plain-language, factual reasons without letting a model assert things about the learner; keeps the existing rule that repeated difficulty needs two separate assessed attempts.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Free-text reasons per step (unverifiable learner claims); keep reorder-3 (what the owner asked to replace).

key_decisions.choice: PARTNER_REPLY_MODE=reaction: the model writes only a short trilingual reaction to what the learner said (≤120 chars per language, no question mark); code appends the authored anchor (cue, accepted+next cue, success, hint). Guard rejects invalid-choice aliases, numbers/weekdays/prices absent from scenario copy and learner text, and shared CONFIRMATION_WORDS when the goal was not accepted; rejection or provider failure → authored reply, turn never fails. A later 'paraphrase' mode (generated cue must keep all fact tokens and ≥0.6 content-word overlap) is gated on the reply_guard eval suite.
key_decisions.why: Facts and the next question always come from authored text, so contradiction by omission is impossible and the guard only has to police one sentence. The interpretation hot path stays one complete_once call.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Fully free reply with the anchor as guidance (cannot verify it still asks the right question without authored tokens); authored only (owner's 'boring' complaint).

key_decisions.decision: Where generated scenarios live and when they appear
key_decisions.choice: Table conversation_scenarios (blueprint JSONB + validator report + status). Authored content/conversations/pilot.json stays static. Admin batches go generate → validate → review queue → publish. On-demand requests become visible to the requester once code validation passes, labelled generated/unreviewed, and also enter the queue.
key_decisions.why: The container must not write lesson files (rule kept). Mirrors D-18: validated generated story episodes are shown unreviewed with a label.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Writing JSON into content/ at runtime; fully runtime-improvised scenarios with no stored blueprint (no validate_meaning anchors, nothing to review).

key_decisions.decision: How tests script tool calls and streams
key_decisions.choice: chat_replies.json entry {'script':[{'tool_calls':[{'name':..,'arguments':{..}}]},…,{'final':{..}}]} selected by prompt_version and indexed by the number of assistant tool-call turns already in messages (stateless, safe for the long-lived e2e process). Placeholders: existing $last plus $tool.<name>.<path> to copy ids out of earlier tool results. Optional 'chunks' and 'fail_after_chunks' for stream(). pytest may inject a callable(messages, tools). Fixture-produced judgements are never recorded as mistakes or assessed outcomes.
key_decisions.why: Deterministic multi-step runs without a model, and no hidden per-instance state between Playwright tests.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Counter on the fixture instance (leaks across e2e tests); recorded cassettes (brittle, contain prompts).

key_decisions.choice: Bicep defaults: dailyModelCalls 80→250, dailyTokens 80000→300000, totalModelCalls 2000→15000, totalTokens 2000000→15000000; chatCapacity 1→50 (small) and 30 (strong), quota permitting. Code sub-budgets in domains/llm/budgets.py: tutor 3 steps/3500 tokens, follow-up 2/2500, guide 4/7000 (3 runs/day), partner reply 1 call/900, feedback 1 call/2500, scenario 2 calls/12000 (3/day), tutor threads 30/day.
key_decisions.why: Estimated typical day ≈ 87k tokens/75 calls (guide 6k, two conversations 26k, six explains 15k, four follow-ups 6k, two writing reviews 8k, story 8k, ten mission turns 18k); heavy day ≈ 130k/120 calls. Capacity 1 means 1k TPM, which a single 2k-token agent step already exceeds.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Keeping 80/80k (the study guide plus one conversation would exhaust it); removing caps for the owner (breaks D-07/D-17).

open_risks: Stance weakness 1 — protocol ownership: the Responses item types, SSE event names and the encrypted-reasoning echo are maintained by us. Mitigation: ignore unknown items/events, contract tests with recorded payloads, AZURE_CHAT_API=chat_completions rollback while gpt-4.1-mini exists (until 2027-04-14), and the option to swap the adapter internals to the openai SDK without touching domain code.

Stance weakness 2 — features a framework gives for free are absent: session memory abstractions, checkpoint/resume, human-in-the-loop, multi-agent, MCP, ready-made Foundry tracing/eval dashboards. If the product needs them, Tool and AgentSpec port 1:1 to Agent Framework function tools; the loop is the only code discarded.

Stance weakness 3 — hand-rolled GenAI telemetry follows conventions that are still changing; single-maintainer knowledge of the loop; thread-per-stream concurrency (fine for one learner, a ceiling near the 40-thread pool and 10 DB connections for many).

Local development quality: llama3.1:8b tool calling is unreliable and Ollama ignores tool_choice, so local agent runs will often hit the deterministic fallback; agents are verified on scripted fixtures in CI and on Azure by the eval run, not on the laptop model.

Quota: the Azure model page states gpt-5.6 and gpt-6 need quota requests on lower subscription tiers. If refused, deploy gpt-5.4-mini / gpt-5.4 (Data Zone Standard in West Europe, GA until 2027-09). Per-token prices cited in the review (and the cost estimate of roughly 5–15 USD per month at the new caps) were not re-verified against the Azure calculator.

Losing temperature=0.0 on reasoning models may change interpretation consistency; reasoning effort 'none' plus strict schemas should compensate but this is only known after the Azure eval run. Do not cut over without it.

SSE path is unproven in production: Next compression, the Easy Auth sidecar and Container Apps ingress could buffer; BaseHTTPMiddleware could delay disconnect detection under FastAPI 0.141.1 / Starlette 1.6.0. Every streaming endpoint therefore also answers plain JSON, and AGENT_STREAMING_ENABLED can stay off.

Validators are heuristics (substring grounding, deny-lists, vocabulary coverage, token overlap). They can reject good output (higher fallback rate) and cannot prove a Dutch explanation or a Persian/English gloss is correct. Outputs stay labelled generated/unreviewed; measure fallback and rejection rates from agent_runs and tune with the eval suites.

The study guide makes one automatic paid run per day on the first Today visit. It is bounded and switchable, but it is a deliberate departure from 'page views are free'; the owner should confirm this is wanted rather than an explicit button.

Generated scenarios pass code checks, not a teacher. Reachability via validate_meaning proves a goal can be met, not that the Dutch is natural Belgian Standard Dutch; human review remains a separate status and the label must stay visible.

The 'total' usage scope is a lifetime counter; at 300k tokens per day the proposed 15M total lasts about 50 heavy days. Either the owner raises it periodically or a monthly scope is added (not designed here).

Platform issues outside this track still bite: job lease 60 s with no heartbeat (scenario generation uses a 45 s call timeout and max_attempts=1), usage_counters row locks held across provider calls at legacy in-transaction sites, and the conversation row lock now spans two calls (3–5 s; concurrent tabs get the existing 409).

Cross-track coupling: this track needs the learner profile (stage, support language, feature switches via GET /me), record_activity and the Today planner, the exercises generator and learner_mistakes, components/ui primitives and the exercise kit. Migration numbers 0011–0015 are placeholders to be assigned at merge; TodayHome.tsx and TopicConversation.tsx are edited by more than one track.

Default Azure content filters are not trained on Dutch; a content_filter refusal is mapped to a friendly message and the authored fallback, but false blocks on harmless Dutch are possible and not controllable from code.

Stateless tool loops resend the growing input (tool results plus encrypted reasoning items) each step; with effort 'low' and 4 steps the study guide can approach its 7000-token ceiling. The ceiling stops the run and the planner fallback is shown, so the failure mode is cost-bounded but visible.

proposals.approach_summary: Keep the narrow ChatModel port and make it tool-, schema- and stream-capable (respond, stream) while complete/complete_once stay byte-compatible. Azure moves to a hand-written, stateless Responses-API adapter on EU Data Zone deployments, because Microsoft documents that current reasoning models cannot combine tools with Chat Completions; Ollama stays on Chat Completions; the fixture scripts tool calls and chunks per prompt_version. One LlmGateway owns reserve -> call -> settle with deterministic call ids, so a call id is sent at most once and no transaction spans a provider call. Agents are LangGraph 1.2 StateGraphs compiled once: a custom model node calls the port through the gateway, a custom tools node runs typed, learner-scoped read/propose tools, conditional edges bound the loop, recursion_limit plus a checkpointed budget cap it, and langgraph-checkpoint-postgres (schema agent_state) journals every super-step for resume and holds the tutor's short-lived thread. No LangChain chat-model wrapper and no prebuilt ToolNode. Domain tables stay the system of record. A runner thread feeds graph.stream(stream_mode=[custom, updates]) into FastAPI's native EventSourceResponse; only code-validated content is streamed. Tutor, study guide and partner are thin specs on this runtime, each with validators, caches, a flag and a deterministic fallback. Honest weakness: the checkpointer is a second persistence path outside Alembic and SQLAlchemy and still needs our own call ledger; two of the three agents barely loop. De-risking: agents/runtime.py is the only agent module importing langgraph, so the loop can be swapped for plain Python without touching tools, gateway, features or the web.

key_decisions.decision: How the project's ChatModel port maps into the graph
key_decisions.choice: Custom LangGraph nodes call the port through LlmGateway. Graph state carries plain-dict messages in the port's own shape (role, content, tool_calls, tool_call_id, opaque). No LangChain BaseChatModel wrapper, no prebuilt ToolNode or create_agent, no 'messages' stream mode. Nodes emit tokens and progress with langgraph.config.get_stream_writer(); the caller uses graph.stream(input, config, context=RunContext(...), stream_mode=['custom','updates'], version='v2', durability='sync'). Non-serialisable things (gateway, tool registry, learner id, cancel event, settings) travel in LangGraph Runtime context (context_schema, from langgraph.runtime import Runtime), never in checkpointed state.
key_decisions.why: The gateway must be able to refuse before and settle after every single HTTP request; a callback-driven wrapper cannot guarantee that. BaseChatModel brings callbacks (LangSmith export of prompts if an env var is set), with_retry and caches that collide with the at-most-once and no-prompt-telemetry rules. ToolNode requires AIMessage.tool_calls and LangChain tools and feeds raw error text back to the model; our tools need typed context injection, READ ONLY transactions and effect classes. Plain-dict state keeps checkpoints free of msgpack extension types: JsonPlusSerializer today only warns for unregistered types and says they 'will be blocked in a future version' (LANGGRAPH_STRICT_MSGPACK). LangGraph's streaming docs name stream_mode='custom' as the route for non-LangChain LLM clients. Verified from primary sources: langgraph 1.2.12 is locked (1.2.13 current); default recursion_limit is 1000 since 1.0.6, so it must be set explicitly.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: LangChain chat-model wrapper + ToolNode + create_agent: needs the langchain package, hides the loop we are obliged to bound and audit, and makes usage accounting implicit. A plain Python while-loop with no LangGraph: honestly viable and about 150 lines smaller, but gives up checkpoint/resume, stream multiplexing and the graph idiom the repo already uses; kept as the documented exit because only agents/runtime.py and agents/checkpoint.py import langgraph for agents.

key_decisions.decision: What the PostgreSQL checkpointer is for
key_decisions.choice: langgraph-checkpoint-postgres 3.1.x PostgresSaver (requires langgraph-checkpoint >=4.1,<5 - lock has 4.2.0 -, psycopg >=3.2 - lock has 3.3.6 -, orjson - in lock -, and psycopg-pool, which is new) on its own autocommit pool (max 2 connections, row_factory=dict_row, options '-c search_path=agent_state'). Checkpoints are (1) a per-run journal: thread 'run:{run_id}', deleted with delete_thread when the run settles; (2) the model context of a tutor session: thread 'tutor:{session_id}', 24 h idle TTL. Everything the learner sees, exports or deletes lives in FK-cascaded domain tables (tutor_sessions, study_plans, topic_conversations). agent_threads registers every thread so a GC job can remove orphans.
key_decisions.why: Resume after a crash or timeout skips completed super-steps, so already-paid model calls are not paid again; the tutor's follow-ups get their context (tool results, encrypted reasoning items) without a bespoke scratch column; get_state gives a debuggable snapshot of a failed run. Keeping learner-facing truth in domain tables preserves learner-deletion cascade, export and the test-pinned view() of conversations.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Checkpoint as system of record for conversations (opaque format, no FK cascade, breaks export and migrations). A custom BaseCheckpointSaver on the request's SQLAlchemy session (atomic with domain writes, but couples us to put/put_writes/get_tuple/list/delete_thread internals and blob versioning). InMemorySaver only (loses resume on every restart of the single replica).

key_decisions.decision: Checkpoint tables versus the Alembic-only rule
key_decisions.choice: Alembic migration creates schema agent_state; dlp.release.migrate() calls PostgresSaver.setup() on an admin autocommit connection with search_path=agent_state immediately after command.upgrade, then grants USAGE and DML on that schema to dlp_app. /health/ready additionally requires agent_state.checkpoint_migrations. tests/conftest.py runs the same setup after 'alembic upgrade head'.
key_decisions.why: The library hard-codes unqualified table names (checkpoint_migrations, checkpoints, checkpoint_blobs, checkpoint_writes), versions them itself (10 internal migrations today) and uses CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, which cannot run inside Alembic's transaction. Copying its DDL into our migrations would drift on every library bump. Release stays migration-first and the runtime role stays DML-only.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Copying the DDL into an Alembic revision; calling setup() at API startup (needs DDL rights on the runtime role); putting the tables in public (name collisions, noisy grants).

key_decisions.decision: Azure adapter: API, SDK, state, reasoning, token accounting
key_decisions.choice: New hand-written httpx adapter AzureResponsesChatModel on {endpoint}/openai/v1/responses with the existing managed-identity token provider (scope https://ai.azure.com/.default). Stateless: store:false, no previous_response_id; reasoning items (encrypted_content is returned by default in stateless mode) are echoed back verbatim through ChatMessage.opaque. reasoning.effort is sent explicitly on every request (none for interpret/reply, low for diagnosis/planning, medium for drafts and writing feedback); max_output_tokens; temperature omitted unless AZURE_CHAT_SEND_TEMPERATURE=true; function tools with strict:true; text.format json_schema built by providers/chat_wire.strict_json_schema(). complete() keeps bounded retry/repair/truncation; complete_once(), respond() and stream() send exactly one request. Usage of every attempt is summed into ChatResult.billed_input_tokens/billed_output_tokens (plus cached and reasoning token counts); input_tokens/output_tokens keep their final-attempt meaning for pinned tests.
key_decisions.why: Microsoft's reasoning-models page (updated 2026-09-29) says: use the Responses API when combining reasoning with tools; gpt-5.6 models 'can't combine reasoning with tools on Chat Completions' and gpt-6.1-sol lists tools as 'Responses API only'; reasoning models reject temperature, top_p and max_tokens. Stateless keeps one owner of conversation state and avoids 30-day provider-side storage of learner text. httpx keeps the request-counting tests (httpx.MockTransport in tests/test_single_model_call.py), the never-log-bodies rule and the lock file small.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: openai SDK inside the adapter (allowed by the rules, but hidden retries must be disabled and logging audited); stateful Responses (second store of learner text, harder at-most-once); staying on Chat Completions with reasoning_effort none on tool requests (works for gpt-5.4 today, dead end); Microsoft Agent Framework or Foundry Agent Service (owner chose in-process; Foundry agents lack strict structured outputs).

key_decisions.decision: Azure models, SKU and retirement guard
key_decisions.choice: DataZoneStandard (EU data zone) deployments created side by side: chat-small-2 = gpt-5.4-mini version 2026-03-17 (GA, retires 2027-09-21), chat-strong-2 = gpt-5.4 version 2026-03-05 (GA, retires 2027-09-02), capacity 30 each, versionUpgradeOption stays NoAutoUpgrade. Benchmark candidates before go-live: gpt-5.6-luna / gpt-5.6-terra (retire 2028-01-11, quota request may be needed) and gpt-6-luna (supports temperature, released 2026-09-22). Retirement dates are deploy parameters (chatModelRetiresOn, strongModelRetiresOn) checked by scripts/check_azure_config.py and compared with live ARM data (lifecycleStatus, deprecation.inference from the account models API) by scripts/check_model_lifecycle.py in the release workflow; preflight shows 'chat model lifecycle' ok / expiring (<120 days) / retired; the adapter maps HTTP 410 to ProviderUnavailable('chat deployment retired').
key_decisions.why: Microsoft's region table (2026-09-03) offers regional Standard in westeurope only for gpt-4.1-mini, which is Deprecated and retires 2027-04-14; gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.5, gpt-5.6-* and gpt-6-* are Data Zone Standard there. gpt-5.4(-mini) needs no access or quota request and supports Responses, structured outputs, tools and streaming. scripts/check_azure_config.py already accepts DataZoneStandard. With NoAutoUpgrade a deployment simply stops at retirement, so an explicit guard is required.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: GlobalStandard (processing may leave the EU; GO_LIVE warns against silently choosing it); swapping the model in place on chat-small (no rollback, no A/B benchmark); keeping gpt-4.1-mini until 2027 (no tool calling with reasoning, new subscriptions cannot deploy it).

key_decisions.choice: Ollama keeps OpenAICompatibleChatModel on /v1/chat/completions, extended with respond()/stream(): tools, stream:true with stream_options.include_usage, response_format json_schema with fallback to json_object + schema_instruction. The runtime never depends on tool_choice (Ollama documents it as unsupported): a reply without tool calls is the final answer. FixtureChatModel gains respond()/stream(): a chat_replies.json entry {'script':[{'tool_calls':[{'name':..,'arguments':{..}}]},{'final':{..},'stream':['chunk',..]}]} is indexed by the number of assistant tool-call messages already present, so it is stateless, deterministic and resume-safe; rule tables and '$last' still work per script step; fail_first/fail_calls apply; new fail_mid_stream_after breaks a stream.
key_decisions.why: Keeps local development on llama3.1:8b and CI/Playwright free of paid services, and lets tests script a whole tool loop or a streamed reply by prompt_version exactly as they script single replies today.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: One Responses adapter for both backends (Ollama >= 0.13.3 documents a non-stateful /v1/responses with tools and streaming): less code, but structured-output support there is undocumented; revisit once the adapter contract tests pass against local Ollama. A stateful FakeChatModel with call counters (breaks on resume and across processes).

key_decisions.decision: LlmGateway, at-most-once and the single failure policy
key_decisions.choice: dlp/llm/gateway.py is the only caller of usage.* and of the port. Each request has a deterministic call id '{run_id}:{step}' read from checkpointed state. reserve (model_calls 1 + tokens = input estimate + max_output_tokens) commits in its own short transaction before the request; settle commits after it; no transaction or row lock spans a provider call on agent paths. A reused call id is never sent again: found 'reserved' -> earlier attempt was in flight -> commit the estimate and raise UncertainCall; found 'committed' -> its result was lost before the checkpoint -> UncertainCall; the run ends in its deterministic fallback. Outcomes: not sent (connect error, auth, paid flag off, semaphore timeout), 400/401/403/404/410 and 429 -> release (429 retried once after Retry-After within the deadline); sent and failed, timed out or malformed -> commit estimate; cancelled stream -> input estimate + emitted text + 64; success -> billed tokens of all attempts. RunBudget(max_steps, max_tokens, deadline) is enforced in graph state. Legacy call sites use gateway.call(session=...) inside their request transaction.
key_decisions.why: Implements 'reserved before, settled after, uncertain never silently replayed' by construction instead of eleven hand-written variants, and makes the checkpoint resume safe for paid calls.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: One run-level reservation settled at the end (fewer writes, but cannot tell which call was in flight after a crash); holding the paid-model advisory lock across the loop (blocks every other paid role and keeps a transaction open for the whole run); relying on the checkpoint alone for at-most-once (a crash between provider reply and checkpoint write would replay the call).

key_decisions.decision: What may be streamed to the learner
key_decisions.choice: Structured proposals (diagnosis, interpretation, plan, feedback points) are never streamed; code validates them first. Only the phrasing step that follows validated facts is token-streamed (tutor explanation and follow-ups), with a post-stream guard that can emit a 'replace' event carrying an authored text. Partner replies are generated fully, guarded, then sent as one 'reply' event after an early 'interpreted' event (the goal tick appears at once).
key_decisions.why: Models propose, code decides: an unvalidated claim about learner text must not reach the screen and then be withdrawn.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Incremental JSON parsing to stream a field of a structured reply (shows ungrounded quotes before validation); streaming partner replies token by token (short text, and a guard trip would visibly retract a line).

key_decisions.decision: SSE on a synchronous FastAPI app
key_decisions.choice: Sync 'def' generator routes with fastapi.sse.EventSourceResponse / ServerSentEvent (native since FastAPI 0.135; lock has 0.141.1; pyproject lower bound moves to 0.135). A bounded AgentRunner thread pool (AGENT_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS=2) runs the sync graph and pushes AgentEvents into a queue; the route generator only drains the queue and emits a keep-alive comment every 10 s; settlement happens in the runner's finally, independent of the client. Streaming routes use stream_context_dep, not Depends(get_session): FastAPI's default dependency scope keeps a yielded session open until the response has been sent. Every stream route has a JSON twin that drains the same handle. Events: run, status, delta, replace, item, final, error; id = '{run_id}:{seq}'. Disconnect policy per spec: tutor cancels, partner turn and guide finish and cache.
key_decisions.why: No async rewrite, no DB transaction held during a stream, one code path for streamed and non-streamed callers, cooperative cancellation through a threading.Event checked between chunks and before each step.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: async routes with graph.astream (needs async ports and async DB access); WebSocket (Next route handlers cannot accept upgrades); polling a run resource (kept only as the reconnect fallback: GET /agents/runs/{id}).

key_decisions.choice: agents/tools.py Tool(name, description, args_model, effect='read'|'propose', fn(ToolContext, args) -> BaseModel). Arguments are pydantic models with extra='forbid' and never contain learner ids; ToolContext carries learner_id, stage_id, support language, clock and a session factory. Read tools run inside SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY and return trimmed, size-capped JSON (4000 characters). Propose tools run code validators and return {accepted, reasons}; accepted proposals are appended to state.proposals and applied after the run by the feature service or by an explicit learner click. No tool writes a domain table, awards points, changes a schedule or saves a word. stories.service.today_episode and stories.service.library are deliberately not tools (they lock, insert and can enqueue a paid job).
key_decisions.why: Keeps dates, completion, passes, points, schedules and submissions in application code and makes learner scoping a property of the runtime rather than of prompts.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Generic SQL or 'get row by id' tools; write tools with confirmation prompts; exposing existing HTTP routes as tools.

key_decisions.decision: Unifying topic conversations and the mission engine
key_decisions.choice: Share the graph nodes and guard, not the tables or state machines: agents/partner/graph.py has interpret -> validate (pluggable: topic_conversations.workflow.validate_meaning or practice.actions.apply_action) -> reply -> guard. practice/workflow.py reuses partner/guard.py (generalised from _contradicts_decision and CONFIRMATION_WORDS) and is compiled once; service missions keep fixed lines. Both go through the gateway and emit the same event contract.
key_decisions.why: Missions are graded lesson steps with evidence rows, checkpoints and one-attempt rules (D-12, D-13); topic conversations are free practice. Merging their persistence would put pinned behaviour at risk for little gain.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: One conversations table and one engine (large migration, breaks test_turns.py, test_actions.py and test_service_missions.py).

key_decisions.choice: Generated Dutch is never machine-translated silently. Partner reply: reply.nl is generated, reply.en/reply.fa carry the authored anchor line of the code's decision, shown as gist ('In het kort'); an explicit 'Vertaal' button reuses the story-translate-v1 call. Tutor: the model writes the support-language paragraph itself (it is the explanation), labelled as generated and wrapped in lang=fa dir=rtl. Study guide and feedback notes: closed reason/note codes rendered from authored nl/en/fa templates; the optional generated sentence is Dutch only.
key_decisions.why: Keeps the {nl,en,fa} contract of LearningText and PhraseAudio, keeps Persian quality under authored control where possible, and keeps the generated label honest.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: A translation call on every reply (doubles cost and latency); leaving en/fa empty (beginners lose support exactly where they need it).

key_decisions.choice: GET /today never calls a model; it returns the deterministic plan (P3 Today planner) plus the cached guide if one exists. The web POSTs /today/guide once per Brussels day after Today has rendered (only when history exists and the flag is on). Result is cached in study_plans by learner, day and snapshot_version; at most 3 runs per day; fallback results are cached too and may be retried after 30 minutes. Snapshot and candidate activities are preloaded into the first message, so a typical run is two model calls.
key_decisions.why: Preserves the pinned rule that reading the plan is free and the Today page is instant; bounds cost to one small run per day.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Running the agent inside GET /today (slow, paid on page view, breaks tests); a nightly job (the single learner's day starts whenever they open the app; job lease is 60 s without heartbeat).

key_decisions.choice: Estimates (small tier, tokens in+out): partner turn about 2,100 in 2 calls; six-turn conversation with feedback about 14,500 in 13 calls; tutor explanation 2,300-3,800 in 2-3 calls; follow-up about 1,200; study guide about 4,000-5,000 in 2-3 calls. A normal active day (1 guide, 2 conversations, 8 explanations, 6 follow-ups, 1 story, 3 writing/speaking checks) is about 78k tokens and 60 calls - at today's production caps of 80 calls / 80k tokens; a heavy day is about 150k / 110. Raise Bicep defaults to dailyModelCalls 200, dailyTokens 250000, totalModelCalls 20000, totalTokens 30000000, chatCapacity 30. Add per-feature run caps in code: guide 3/day, tutor 40 sessions/day with 4 follow-ups each, feedback 20/day, scenario drafts 10/day (admin); conversations keep MAX_DAILY_STARTS=20.
key_decisions.why: The current caps were sized for single-call roles; agent loops multiply calls. Capacity 1 (1K TPM) would return 429 on the second call of any loop.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Keeping the caps and letting agents fall back most days (owner would rarely see the features); separate usage metrics per feature (schema change with little benefit for one learner). Prices for gpt-5.4-mini/gpt-5.4 were not verified here: read them from the Azure pricing page before approving the caps; under an assumed <= 1 USD per million input and <= 5 USD per million output tokens the 250k cap is roughly 0.4 USD/day.

key_decisions.choice: Settings and Bicep params, all default false, surfaced to the web through GET /me features: AGENT_TUTOR_ENABLED, AGENT_GUIDE_ENABLED, PARTNER_GENERATIVE_REPLIES, CONVERSATION_FEEDBACK_ENABLED, FREE_CONVERSATIONS_ENABLED, AGENT_STREAMING_ENABLED; plus AZURE_CHAT_API (responses|chat_completions) and AGENT_CHECKPOINTER (postgres|memory). Order: gateway (no behaviour change) -> port v2 + fixture + Ollama -> Azure Responses adapter still pointing at gpt-4.1-mini -> new deployments benchmarked and switched -> runtime + checkpointer + SSE -> tutor -> study guide -> generative partner replies on the ten pilots -> feedback -> generated scenarios -> free conversations. Each flag is turned on in production only after the on-demand Azure eval meets its thresholds and the result is recorded in DECISIONS.md.
key_decisions.why: Every step is independently reviewable and reversible by an environment variable; the riskiest surface (free generative conversation) comes last.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Big-bang switch of adapter, model and agents together.

key_decisions.choice: agents/partner exposes voice_session_instructions(blueprint) and validate_transcript_turn(blueprint, step_index, transcript) so a Voice Live session can use the same facts ledger and code-validated goals; LlmGateway accepts other metrics (a future voice_seconds) through the same reserve/settle; agent_runs.kind allows 'voice_session'; the AgentEvent/SSE contract and the features map are reusable; partner/guard.py works on any reply text.
key_decisions.why: Voice needs scenario grounding, goal validation, usage accounting and audit, not a second implementation of them.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Designing the WebSocket bridge here (owned by the voice track).

key_decisions.decision: Real weaknesses of the LangGraph-native stance (accepted, with mitigations)
key_decisions.choice: (1) Second persistence path: checkpoints are written on a separate autocommit connection, not atomic with domain writes, outside Alembic; mitigated by schema isolation, release-time setup and domain tables as system of record. (2) The checkpointer does not by itself give at-most-once for paid calls; we still need the usage-reservation call ledger. (3) Dependency churn: four packages (langgraph, langgraph-checkpoint, langgraph-checkpoint-postgres, langgraph-prebuilt) plus transitive langchain-core and langsmith; defaults have changed within 1.x (recursion limit 1000, stream version v2, msgpack strictness); mitigated by tests/test_langgraph_contract.py and the hashed lock. (4) Because we refuse the LangChain wrapper we use only StateGraph, conditional edges, Runtime context, the checkpointer and stream multiplexing - roughly what a 150-line loop would replace. (5) Sync graphs mean one thread per run and cooperative cancellation only. (6) Tutor checkpoints hold learner text outside FK cascade for up to 24 h; mitigated by agent_threads + GC and by never storing conversations there. (7) durability='sync' adds a few database round trips per super-step on a 0.25 vCPU replica. (8) Study guide and partner turn are near-linear pipelines; only the tutor really loops.
key_decisions.why: Stated so the synthesiser can weigh the stance; none is disqualifying for one learner and one replica.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Hiding these behind the 'already installed' argument: only langgraph core is installed; the Postgres checkpointer and psycopg-pool are new.

open_risks: Stance risk: the Postgres checkpointer is a second persistence path (own pool, autocommit, library-managed DDL, no FK cascade) whose main benefit here - resume without re-paying - only matters after rare crashes, and it does not remove the need for our own call ledger. If the synthesiser prefers a plain loop, drop agents/checkpoint.py, keep tutor context in tutor_sessions, and everything else in this plan (port v2, gateway, tools, SSE, features) stands unchanged.

LangGraph API facts were verified from the current docs (stream modes, get_stream_writer, version='v2', Runtime context, durability modes, recursion limit 1000 since 1.0.6, PostgresSaver setup/kwargs, table DDL, JsonPlusSerializer strictness) but not executed in this worktree; the durable-execution page could not be fetched, so the exact resume semantics (re-execution starts at the first unfinished node of the interrupted super-step) must be proven by tests/test_agent_checkpoint.py before relying on it.

Azure facts come from Microsoft Learn pages dated July-September 2026: West Europe availability by SKU, retirement dates, the tool-calling restriction on Chat Completions, stateless reasoning items. Subscription quota, the exact Responses wire shapes (text.format nesting, usage field names), the default reasoning effort of gpt-5.4-mini and whether the Bicep deployments API version 2024-10-01 accepts DataZoneStandard for these models need a what-if and one recorded live call.

Prices for gpt-5.4-mini and gpt-5.4 were not verified; the raised caps (200 calls, 250k tokens per day) must be approved against the Azure pricing page. Reasoning tokens are billed as output and count against max_output_tokens, so 'low' effort calls need headroom and cost more than the estimates if the model reasons longer.

Temperature is not accepted by gpt-5.x reasoning models: the story writer (0.7) and character replies (0.3) lose that lever when the deployment switches. Variety has to come from prompt inputs; if episodes become repetitive, evaluate gpt-6-luna (temperature supported) for the strong tier.

Free-form Dutch grammar explanations and 'better form' suggestions are generated and reviewed by nobody qualified. Code can guarantee grounding of quotes and agreement with answer keys, not linguistic correctness. They stay labelled as generated, capped, and gated by evals; a wrong rule explained confidently is the main pedagogical risk of the tutor.

The partner reply guard is heuristic (markers, number/time/name extraction, vocabulary coverage). It can let through a subtly wrong but plausible sentence and will reject some good ones; proper nouns and Dutch compound words make the facts check noisy. Guard-trip rate and a manual review of 50 live replies should precede enabling the flag beyond the ten pilots.

Streaming behind the real stack is unproven: Next's compression, the Easy Auth sidecar and Container Apps ingress could buffer or cut idle streams (ingress idle timeout about 240 s). Mitigations are in place (no-transform, 10 s keep-alives, JSON twin fallback, live probe) but only a live run settles it.

Sync execution model: one thread per run, cooperative cancellation only, and a streamed call holds a slot of the per-model semaphore (max_concurrent_model_calls=2) while the in-process job loop may want it for a story episode. Semaphore acquisition gets a timeout tied to the run deadline; on a 0.25 vCPU replica two concurrent runs plus a job are the practical ceiling.

Starlette's function-middleware (BaseHTTPMiddleware) and client-disconnect propagation for streaming responses were not verified for starlette 1.6.0; the plan replaces request_metadata with a pure ASGI middleware, which touches every response and must keep the four headers identical (covered by tests, but it is a cross-cutting change).

Dependencies on other tracks: learner snapshot and Today planner (P3), exercises generator and learner_mistakes (P4), GET /me features and profile stage (P2), exercise kit and design primitives (P1/P4 web). Tutor drill, mistake memory and guide candidates degrade to 'not available' if those seams slip; migration numbers 0011-0015 must be renumbered at merge.

Job lease: scenario drafts run in the 60 s-lease job loop without heartbeat. The draft deadline is set to 45 s per attempt; if the strong model with medium reasoning is slower, the job needs the heartbeat planned in P8 or drafts must run from the CLI only.

llama3.1:8b tool calling is unreliable and Ollama ignores tool_choice; local agent runs will often fall back. Local development proves plumbing, not behaviour; behavioural evidence comes only from the on-demand Azure eval.

Checkpoints of tutor threads hold learner text for up to 24 h plus the GC interval outside the FK cascade, and appear in database backups. If that is unacceptable, set the tutor thread TTL to the request (journal only) and reseed each follow-up from tutor_sessions.turns - a configuration change, at the cost of resending tool context.

Generated Persian in tutor explanations is model-written and unreviewed; RTL markup is enforced, quality is not. If quality is poor, switch the support paragraph to authored category notes plus an optional on-demand translation.

proposals.approach_summary: Keep the project's ports as the only seam and put Microsoft Agent Framework (agent-framework-core 1.20.0 + agent-framework-openai 1.15.0, Python >=3.10, GA since 2 Apr 2026) behind them in two adapter modules. ChatModel v2 (tools, tool-role messages, strict output, one-request complete_step/stream) stays in providers/base.py; the Azure adapter becomes AF's OpenAIChatClient (Responses API, store=False, max_retries=0), Ollama stays on the extended httpx client, fixtures gain scripted tool calls and chunked streams. A new AgentRunner port is implemented by an AF Agent whose chat and function middleware enforce a pre-reserved per-run budget and a learner-scoped tool registry (read tools plus code-validated propose tools); in fixture and Ollama mode the same AF loop runs over a small bridge client, so CI exercises the real loop. One LlmGateway owns reserve, call, settle, one failure policy and a metadata-only agent_runs table. AF is async and the app is sync: one agent-loop thread owns all AF clients; only SSE routes are async def. Streaming uses FastAPI's built-in SSE plus AF ResponseStream gates, so nothing unvalidated reaches the browser. Tutor, study guide and conversation feedback are bounded agent runs with deterministic fallbacks; the partner turn stays a two-call pipeline (strict interpret, code decides, guarded generative bridge plus authored cue). Azure moves to DataZoneStandard gpt-5.x on Responses: West Europe regional Standard only offers deprecated gpt-4.1-mini, and gpt-5.6 rejects function tools on Chat Completions unless reasoning is off.

key_decisions.decision: Where Agent Framework sits relative to the ports rule
key_decisions.choice: Domain code sees only providers/base.py: ChatModel (v2) and a new sync AgentRunner port with project types (AgentSpec, ToolSpec, ToolContext, AgentRunResult). agent_framework and openai are imported only in providers/chat_azure_responses.py, providers/agent_af.py and providers/async_bridge.py; tests/test_architecture.py fails on any other import. agent-framework-core is a normal dependency (the loop runs in CI too); agent-framework-openai lives in the azure extra and is imported lazily like azure.identity today.
key_decisions.why: Keeps ENGINEERING.md's rule literally true, keeps the exit cost bounded (about 600 lines of adapters; ChatModel v2 exists regardless), and lets fixture CI run the real loop, middleware and tool invocation rather than a fake runner.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: AF types used directly in domains (fast, but couples every validator and test to Message/Content and breaks the ports rule). AF only as a transport under ChatModel with a hand-written loop (loses middleware, sessions, ResponseStream gates and GenAI spans, which are the parts worth buying). The agent-framework meta package (pulls every integration).

key_decisions.decision: Why Agent Framework at all (strongest honest case)
key_decisions.choice: Use AF for: the Responses wire protocol (function_call/function_call_output items, automatic reasoning.encrypted_content replay when store=False, strict json_schema conversion from pydantic, streaming events, usage incl. reasoning and cached tokens), per-model-call chat middleware and per-tool function middleware as the enforcement hooks, AgentSession/ContextProvider, ResponseStream update/result gates, and GenAI-semconv spans (invoke_agent, chat, execute_tool; gen_ai.client.token.usage).
key_decisions.why: Verified on learn.microsoft.com and the repo: chat middleware runs for every model call inside the tool loop; RawOpenAIChatClient accepts async_client (so max_retries=0 is ours to set) and adds reasoning.encrypted_content automatically without service-side storage; ResponseStream has with_update_gate/with_result_gate/buffer_updates, which is exactly 'code validates before display'. Hand-writing this against /openai/v1/responses in httpx is 400-600 lines that must track a moving API; AF 1.x is Microsoft's supported path and the same abstractions reach Voice Live and Foundry later.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Hand-rolled loop over ChatModel v2 (about 200 lines, zero dependencies, fully sync - the honest runner-up and the documented exit path). LangGraph prebuilt agents (already a dependency, but no Responses client, no Azure-aligned telemetry, and the plan removes LangGraph). Foundry Agent Service (owner excluded it; no strict structured outputs).

key_decisions.choice: Responses API at {endpoint}/openai/v1/responses through agent_framework.openai.OpenAIChatClient built with async_client=AsyncOpenAI(base_url=.../openai/v1, api_key=<existing _chat_token_provider callable>, max_retries=0, timeout=httpx.Timeout(connect=5, read=chat_timeout_seconds)). Stateless: store=False on every request, no previous_response_id, no Conversations API; continuation items live only in process memory for one run. Selected by AZURE_CHAT_API=responses; the httpx Chat Completions path remains for Ollama and as rollback.
key_decisions.why: Microsoft's reasoning doc states gpt-5.6 fails with tools on /v1/chat/completions unless reasoning_effort is none ('use /v1/responses'); Responses default store=true keeps content 30 days, which a learner's Dutch text should not be; max_retries=0 is required for 'uncertain paid calls are never silently replayed'. Reusing the token callable preserves the live-verified scope https://ai.azure.com/.default.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: credential= on the AF client (AF picks its own scope and the SDK keeps 2 hidden retries). Stateful previous_response_id (fewer input tokens, but server-side retention of learner text and an authorization surface the docs warn about). Staying on Chat Completions with reasoning_effort none (works today, loses reasoning for tutor/guide and is the deprecated direction).

key_decisions.decision: Model tiers and SKU in West Europe
key_decisions.choice: SKU DataZoneStandard (EU data zone), never Global. Small tier: gpt-5.4-mini 2026-03-17 (GA, retires 2027-09-21) as the safe default, gpt-5.6-luna 2026-07-09 (retires 2028-01-11) if the benchmark and price favour it. Strong tier: gpt-5.6-terra or gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-09. versionUpgradeOption stays NoAutoUpgrade. Reasoning effort per prompt: none for interpret/partner reply, low for tutor/guide/feedback, medium for scenario writer and writing corrections. temperature is dropped when the capability profile says unsupported.
key_decisions.why: Region table (checked 2026-10-05): West Europe regional Standard lists only gpt-4.1-mini (Deprecated, retires 2027-04-14); DataZoneStandard in westeurope lists gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-5.5, gpt-5.6-luna/sol/terra, gpt-6-luna/sol, gpt-6.1-sol. Reasoning models other than GPT-6 Astra reject temperature and max_tokens.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Keep Standard gpt-4.1-mini (no migration now, forced one before April 2027 with no regional successor). GlobalStandard (broadest availability, processing outside the EU). gpt-6 family (newest, but quota requests on lower tiers and three weeks old).

key_decisions.decision: Async framework in a sync app
key_decisions.choice: providers/async_bridge.py runs one daemon thread with one asyncio loop that owns every AF client and Agent. Sync callers (routes in the threadpool, the job loop, the CLI, evals) use submit(coro).result(timeout); streams cross threads through a queue; contextvars are copied so spans keep their parent. Tool handlers are sync and run in the executor with their own short read-only session. Only SSE routes are async def.
key_decisions.why: AF docs: a client may not be shared across OS threads or event loops. One owner loop satisfies that for the API process, pytest, CLI and jobs alike, and leaves the other 60-odd sync routes and SQLAlchemy sessions untouched.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Convert the app to async (rewrites every route and the session layer). asyncio.run per call (a new client and connection pool per call, breaks token caching). Run AF on the server loop (job loop and CLI have no server loop).

key_decisions.decision: Budget and reservation model for multi-step runs
key_decisions.choice: LlmGateway.open_run reserves the whole budget up front (model_calls = max_steps, tokens = max_total_tokens) in its own committed transaction and inserts agent_runs(status reserved, lease). BudgetChatMiddleware checks and meters every model call in memory and terminates the run when steps, tokens, deadline or the cancel flag are hit. settle_run commits measured usage once. Budgets: tutor-explain 4 steps/12k tokens/40 s; tutor-followup 3/8k/30 s; study-guide 4/14k/45 s; conversation-feedback 3/10k/40 s.
key_decisions.why: A reservation must be durable before the first paid request (existing rule, stories/service.py:255-287). AF's own max_iterations/max_function_calls are documented as best effort and trigger an extra summarising call, so they are only the soft second line.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Reserve per step inside middleware (N transactions from the loop thread, and a run can die half-paid at the daily cap). Trust AF limits alone (not a hard ceiling).

key_decisions.choice: ProviderUnavailable means provably nothing was sent (connect refused, token acquisition failed, 401/403/404) and releases. Every other ProviderError after a request left the process commits: requests actually made, and measured tokens or the estimate for the unknown attempt. Validation failures after a successful call commit real usage. Cancelled runs commit completed steps plus the in-flight step's estimate. HTTP: 429 allowance, 503 unavailable, 502 uncertain; the practice 502 body with turn/session is kept.
key_decisions.why: Today missions and writing refund on any failure while conversations, coach and review keep the charge; a timeout is billable, so refunding under-counts. One rule is also what agents need.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Always release (under-counts paid timeouts). Always commit (charges learners when Ollama or the endpoint is simply down).

key_decisions.decision: Tools: read-only or propose, never write
key_decisions.choice: ToolSpec(kind=read|propose, input_model pydantic, max_calls). learner_id comes only from ToolContext set by the server and is never a model argument. Read tools run under SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY in their own session. Propose tools validate arguments against run-local state (ids served earlier in this run, substring grounding) and return {accepted, reason_code}; accepted proposals are collected in memory and persisted by the domain service after the run with its normal validation.
key_decisions.why: Preserves 'models propose, code decides' inside a loop and makes at-most-once trivial: replaying or abandoning a run has no side effects. In-loop rejection lets the model fix an ungrounded quote within the step ceiling instead of a blind repair retry.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Write tools with approval (AF supports approval_mode, but a learner approving database writes is not a learning interaction). A generic SQL or search tool (explicitly ruled out).

key_decisions.choice: The same POST that creates the turn returns text/event-stream when Accept asks for it (fastapi.sse.EventSourceResponse, FastAPI >= 0.135; lock has 0.141.1), otherwise JSON from the same pipeline. Events: run, status, delta, replace, final, error with id run:seq and 15 s pings. Deltas are released per sentence only after deterministic update gates pass; final is the fully validated payload and is authoritative. Idempotent on client_message_id; Last-Event-ID replays from an in-process buffer; a completed run replays only final. Routes use stream_context_dep, not Depends(get_session).
key_decisions.why: FastAPI runs yield-dependency teardown after the response is sent, so a request-scoped session would stay open (and idle in transaction) for the whole stream. Single POST keeps abort = cancel = stop paying. Gating by sentence gives real latency gains without ever showing text that code later retracts for a grounding failure.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Raw token streaming (shows unvalidated claims). POST then GET EventSource (two requests, cannot send X-Request-Id, cancel needs a separate call). Sync generator in the threadpool (FastAPI supports it, but disconnects do not close the generator deterministically).

key_decisions.decision: Conversation partner is a pipeline, not a tool loop
key_decisions.choice: Per learner turn: (1) strict interpret via complete_once (topic-conversation-intent-v2, 400 tokens); (2) code validates the goal exactly as validate_meaning does now; (3) one streamed reply call (partner-reply-v1) that writes only a short in-character bridge (<=160 chars) reacting to the learner, to which code appends the authored cue; guard failure or outage falls back to today's authored line. reply_mode 'free' (whole reply generated, must contain a cue anchor) only from B1.
key_decisions.why: A tool hop per turn doubles latency in a dialogue and the facts fit in the prompt. Authored cues keep every question vetted and goals checkable; the bridge supplies the responsiveness the owner misses. D-12's reason for two calls still holds.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: One call that decides and replies (rejected in D-12; reply would have to be parsed to learn what the model did). Fully generative partner at all levels (guard cannot bound invented facts for beginners). An AF agent with scenario tools (latency and cost with no added safety).

key_decisions.choice: Tutor threads use AF AgentSession; session.to_dict() is stored in tutor_threads.af_session with the AF version, but tutor_threads.messages is the canonical transcript and the rebuild source when from_dict fails. A LearnerSnapshotProvider(ContextProvider) injects the SQL-derived snapshot and top mistake categories before each run. 'Memory of recurring error types' is learner_mistakes rows aggregated by SQL, not vector or file memory.
key_decisions.why: Uses the framework's session and context-provider seams while keeping learner data in Postgres rows that cascade on delete and appear in the export; deterministic memory can be explained and tested.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Service-managed history (retention in Azure). AF FileMemoryProvider or Mem0 (model decides what to remember about a learner; not auditable). Persisting only AF session blobs (format is framework-internal and has changed across releases).

key_decisions.choice: chat_replies.json entries gain a 'script' form: a list of steps, the step chosen by counting assistant tool-call turns already in the messages (stateless, concurrency-safe), each step either tool_calls or a reply (rule tables and $last still work; $tool:<name>.<path> echoes ids returned by tools). stream() chunks at whitespace; fail_mid_stream_after injects a broken stream. Ollama gets tools and SSE on the existing httpx adapter; AF drives both through PortChatClient(BaseChatClient).
key_decisions.why: One fixture mechanism for single calls, loops and streams keeps Playwright and pytest free of paid services, and existing monkeypatches of complete/complete_once keep working because single-call sites do not change method.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: agent-framework-ollama (still --pre). A fake AgentRunner in CI (would not exercise middleware or budgets). Recorded Azure cassettes (drift, and learner-like text in the repo).

key_decisions.choice: Enable AF instrumentation with sensitive data off; add an allow-list span processor that keeps only gen_ai.operation.name, gen_ai.provider.name, request/response model, gen_ai.usage.*, gen_ai.tool.name, error.type and dlp.run_kind/prompt_version/outcome/steps; production settings refuse ENABLE_SENSITIVE_DATA=true; set AGENT_FRAMEWORK_FEATURE_MASK_DISABLED=true. A canary test proves no prompt, learner text, tool argument or result is exported.
key_decisions.why: The docs' own trace example shows gen_ai.request.instructions on invoke_agent without sensitive data; the project rule forbids exporting prompts. The canary test turns an AF upgrade that adds attributes into a CI failure.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Disable AF instrumentation and hand-emit spans (safe, but discards the maintained span tree). Trust ENABLE_SENSITIVE_DATA=false alone.

key_decisions.choice: Remove it in the last step: practice/workflow.py and topic_conversations/workflow.py become thin adapters over domains/conversations/pipeline.py (three plain function calls).
key_decisions.why: Two linear three-node graphs compiled per call do not justify a second orchestration dependency (langgraph, langgraph-checkpoint, langgraph-prebuilt, langgraph-sdk, langchain-core in the lock) next to Agent Framework.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Port the graphs to AF workflows (a framework for a three-line sequence). Keep both frameworks.

open_risks: Stance weakness - async framework in a sync app: Agent Framework is async-only and its clients must not cross threads or event loops, so the plan owns a loop-thread bridge (about 150 lines of concurrency code) and tools hop back to worker threads for SQL. Bugs here show up as hangs, not exceptions. Mitigation: bridge tests for cancel, timeout and failure, a wall-clock deadline on every submit, and the bridge is the only place threads meet the loop.

Stance weakness - release cadence: 1.0 on 2 Apr 2026, 1.20 on 2 Oct 2026, and the 2026 changes page lists many renames (clients, sessions, middleware signatures) and post-GA deprecations. API names in this plan were read from docs and source, not executed. Mitigation: A04 starts as a spike, exact versions pinned in the hashed lock, upgrades only with the eval suite and canary test.

Stance weakness - small share of the framework used: Agent loop, function tools, middleware, sessions, ResponseStream gates, telemetry and the Responses client; workflows, multi-agent, MCP, hosted tools and harness stay unused. A hand-written loop over ChatModel v2 would be about 200 lines with no new dependency; it remains the documented exit and should be chosen if the A04 spike exceeds its time box.

Stance weakness - defaults that must be overridden: instrumentation on by default and gen_ai.request.instructions on agent spans; a feature-usage token added to the User-Agent sent to Azure; Responses store defaults to true server-side; the OpenAI SDK retries twice by default; tools run concurrently by default; an in-memory history provider can be auto-added. Each is set explicitly and asserted in tests, but a missed default leaks data or double-bills.

Stance weakness - AF limits are best effort and add a final model call when reached; the hard ceiling is our chat middleware. If a future AF version invokes the model outside the chat-middleware path, the budget would be bypassed - the request-count tests in A06 are the tripwire.

Stance weakness - two transports behind one loop: Azure uses AF's Responses client directly while fixture and Ollama go through PortChatClient. Reasoning-item replay, strict schemas and streaming events are therefore only exercised live; CI cannot catch regressions there. The on-demand Azure eval run before every flag flip is mandatory, not optional.

Stance weakness - local parity is partial: llama3.1:8b tool calling is unreliable and has no strict schema, so local agent runs will often end in the deterministic fallback; AF's native Ollama package is still pre-release, hence the hand-extended httpx adapter.

Dependency weight on a 0.25 vCPU replica: agent-framework-core, openai, msgspec, regex and friends lengthen cold start and the lock file; measure import time in A04 and keep agent-framework-openai lazily imported.

Model choice is not finished: availability and retirement dates were verified (West Europe DataZoneStandard has gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-5.5, gpt-5.6-luna/terra/sol, gpt-6-luna/sol), but prices, the relative roles of luna/terra/sol, whether mini variants accept reasoning effort none, and Dutch quality at effort none were not. Reasoning models ignore temperature, so the story writer loses its 0.7 diversity knob - compensate with code-chosen style seeds and compare with the benchmark.

DataZoneStandard means processing in any EU region rather than only West Europe; GO_LIVE currently promises regional processing. The owner should accept this explicitly in the new DECISIONS entry; the only regional alternative is a deprecated model retiring 2027-04-14.

Streaming through the real stack is unverified: Next compression, the Easy Auth sidecar and Container Apps ingress (240 s request limit) may buffer or cut event streams, and the BaseHTTPMiddleware in main.py may mask disconnects. The JSON variant of every streaming endpoint is the fallback and must stay first-class.

Failure-policy change is user-visible: missions and writing feedback used to refund allowance on any failure and will now keep a conservative charge after timeouts. Combined with reserving whole run budgets, a learner near the daily cap can be refused earlier than before; caps must be raised before the first flag is enabled.

Usage counters remain application estimates: a process crash between a paid request and settlement leaves an agent run 'running' until its lease expires and is then charged in full; exactly-once billing is not claimed and reconciliation against Azure billing stays an owner check.

Sentence-gated streaming with structured output needs an incremental JSON string-field extractor and relies on strict schemas emitting keys in schema order; if that proves brittle the feature flag AGENT_STREAM_DELTAS turns deltas off and only status plus final are sent.

Generated Dutch reaches the learner without human review in three places (tutor explanations, partner bridges, generated scenarios). Deterministic guards catch ungrounded quotes, forbidden claims and contradicted facts, not unnatural or wrong Dutch; labels stay, and qualified Belgian-Dutch review remains a separate owner check as today.

Cross-track dependencies: the snapshot, tutor drill and mistake memory need the profile, activity and exercise seams from P2-P4, and the web steps need the design primitives, exercise kit, TanStack Query and UI-copy catalogue. If those slip, A07 degrades to existing tables and A11/A12/A14 web work waits; migration numbers must be assigned at merge time because several tracks add revisions after 0007.

Mutual exclusion of paid work is weaker across mechanisms: legacy single calls use a transaction-scoped advisory lock while agent runs use a row lease; paid_model_guard is extended to see live leases, but a legacy call that starts just before open_run commits can overlap for one request. Acceptable for a single learner; revisit if the allowlist grows.

scores.verdict: Winner. Keeps every invariant literally testable with httpx.MockTransport and a scripted fixture, adds no dependency and removes one (LangGraph), stays fully synchronous. Weak points: owns Responses wire-format drift and hand-rolled telemetry names; two of its guards collide with pinned tests (AST guard on chat calls, audit row per legacy call with session=None); generator-owned stream settlement is not disconnect-safe; thin voice hooks. All fixable by grafts.

Best ideas on streaming (native FastAPI SSE, twin routes, runner thread that settles regardless of the client) and the most rigorous per-call ledger, but the Postgres checkpointer is a second persistence path outside Alembic and FK cascade, holds learner text 24 h, adds psycopg-pool plus the langchain tree, and by its own admission replaces about 150 lines of loop; resume semantics were never verified. Default model (gpt-5.4-mini) retires 2027-09-21.

Strongest Azure alignment, telemetry and voice hooks, and its repository references are accurate. But an async-only framework in a sync app needs an owned event-loop thread, the Azure transport is exercised only live (fixture and Ollama go through a bridge), several defaults must be overridden to keep the rules (SDK retries, store, instrumentation of instructions, concurrent tools, best-effort limits), and it ships a minor release about every nine days. Too much surface for a solo owner; kept as the documented exit path.
