Nothing was executed; this is a read-only plan.
final_design.approach_summary: Base: the in-house loop. No agent framework; LangGraph is removed. P5: (1) LlmGateway: one reserve/call/settle path and one attempt-accurate failure policy under all eleven call sites; pipelines keep receiving a chat object (a metering proxy), so pinned workflow tests stay valid. (2) ChatModel v2 beside untouched complete/complete_once: respond() (one request, tools, strict schema) and stream(); scripted stateless fixture; Ollama through Chat Completions tools. (3) A hand-written httpx Azure adapter on the stateless Responses API (store:false, explicit reasoning effort, encrypted reasoning replay), then side-by-side EU Data Zone deployments (gpt-5.6-luna/terra; fallback gpt-5.4-mini/5.4) behind an eval gate and a retirement check. (4) A roughly 200-line runtime: whole-run budget reserved and audited in agent_runs before the first call, read-only learner-scoped tools, propose tools validated by code, one repair, deterministic fallback, never replayed. (5) FastAPI's native SSE through the proxy, driven by a runner thread that settles usage independently of the client. (6) GenAI spans with an allow-list and a canary test; an eval harness on the production prompts. P6: tutor (authored explanation first, model for why-follow-ups, grounded quote, drill on click, remembered error categories); study guide (model picks candidate ids and reason codes, code writes the reasons, daily cache, planner fallback); partner (interpret, code validates, Dutch reaction plus authored anchor behind a guard, cited feedback, generated scenarios through validation and a review queue). Every feature has a flag, a JSON twin and a deterministic fallback.

key_decisions.choice: In-house loop in domains/agents/runtime.py on the ChatModel port. No Agent Framework, no LangGraph agents, no Foundry agents.
key_decisions.why: The hard part is the product's invariants (reserve before call, one request per step, at-most-once, body-free logs, substring grounding). They are asserted today with httpx.MockTransport and a fixture; a framework client owns retries, streaming and telemetry, so each invariant becomes middleware against internals re-verified on every upgrade. Scope is three agents, at most four steps, one replica, a synchronous stack. Tool and AgentSpec map 1:1 onto framework function tools if the owner ever switches.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Agent Framework 1.x in-process (async bridge thread, nine-day release cadence, defaults to override, Azure path only testable live). LangGraph with the Postgres checkpointer (second persistence path outside Alembic and FK cascade, new packages, replaces about 150 lines). Foundry hosted agents (excluded by the owner; no strict outputs).

key_decisions.choice: Remove it. Both run_turn graphs become three sequential calls; practice keeps build_graph(chat).invoke(state) as a tiny pipeline object.
key_decisions.why: Both graphs are linear, compiled per call, with no conditional edge or checkpointer; the dependency pulls langgraph, langgraph-checkpoint, langgraph-prebuilt, langgraph-sdk, langchain-core, langchain-protocol and langsmith into the hash-pinned image.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Keep it for two linear graphs; grow it into the agent runtime.

key_decisions.choice: Additive only in providers/base.py: Role gains 'tool'; ChatMessage gains tool_calls, tool_call_id, opaque (defaults); ToolCall, ToolSpec(name, description, parameters: type[BaseModel]), TextDelta, Completed; ChatResult gains tool_calls, finish_reason, requests, reasoning_tokens, cached_tokens, billed_input_tokens, billed_output_tokens, opaque after raw; ProviderError gains uncertain_requests (default 1; ProviderUnavailable 0) and billed_tokens. New non-abstract respond(messages, *, tools=(), tool_choice='auto', schema=None, max_output_tokens=400, temperature=0.2, reasoning_effort='none', timeout_seconds=None, prompt_version='v0', request_id='') and stream(same). respond() is exactly one request; without tools the default delegates to complete_once; with tools it raises ProviderUnavailable.
key_decisions.why: complete/complete_once stay byte-identical, so positional ChatResult constructions, the Mock assert_called_once_with, (messages, **kwargs) monkeypatches, duck-typed test interpreters and benchmarks/language/harness.py keep working.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: tools/stream kwargs on complete (breaks pinned call assertions); a second port class; the name complete_step (respond reads better next to stream).

key_decisions.choice: New providers/chat_azure_responses.py, hand-written httpx against POST {endpoint}/openai/v1/responses, stateless: store:false, input rebuilt from our messages each step, encrypted reasoning items echoed through ChatMessage.opaque with reasoning.context=all_turns, strict text.format json_schema, strict function tools, parallel_tool_calls:false, max_output_tokens. Profile per tier: classic (temperature, no reasoning block) or reasoning (explicit effort, no temperature). OpenAICompatibleChatModel stays for Ollama and as AZURE_CHAT_API=chat_completions rollback.
key_decisions.why: Microsoft: gpt-5.6 cannot combine reasoning with tools on Chat Completions and defaults to medium effort; reasoning models reject temperature and max_tokens; stateless mode returns encrypted reasoning by default; store:true keeps learner text at Azure. httpx keeps transport injection for one-request tests, no hidden SDK retries, no SDK body logging, no new hashed dependencies. The classic profile lets the adapter be proven on the existing gpt-4.1-mini deployment first.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: openai SDK inside the adapter (allowed by the rule; revisit if the wire format churns - domain code would not change); previous_response_id or Conversations (second store of learner text); staying on Chat Completions.

key_decisions.choice: Effort is always sent explicitly on reasoning profiles. none: interpretation, translation, partner reaction. low: tutor, follow-up, study guide, conversation feedback, writing corrections, story writer, scenario writer. Tiers: small for interpretation, reaction and guide; strong for tutor, feedback and scenario writer. max_output_tokens is the total cap including reasoning tokens.
key_decisions.why: With effort none the existing ceilings (400/600/1600) keep their meaning. A confidently wrong grammar rule is the tutor's worst failure and volume is low, so it gets the strong tier.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Model default effort (medium on gpt-5.6: truncates 400-token interpretation calls, triples cost); tutor on the small tier by default (kept as AGENT_TUTOR_TIER=small if evals allow).

key_decisions.choice: DataZoneStandard (EU) in West Europe, side-by-side deployments switched by activeSmallDeployment/activeStrongDeployment. Target: gpt-5.6-luna (small) and gpt-5.6-terra (strong), version as reported by the Models API. Quota fallback: gpt-5.4-mini 2026-03-17 / gpt-5.4 2026-03-05. versionUpgradeOption stays NoAutoUpgrade, guarded by scripts/check_model_lifecycle.py and a preflight item.
key_decisions.why: Verified 2026-10-06: regional Standard in westeurope offers only gpt-4.1-mini (Deprecated, retires 2027-04-14); the listed models are Data Zone Standard there; gpt-5.6 retires 2028-01-11, gpt-5.4-mini 2027-09-21. NoAutoUpgrade keeps an unvetted model out of production but stops at retirement, hence the guard.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: GlobalStandard (processing leaves the EU); in-place model swap (no rollback or A/B eval); gpt-6 family (two weeks old, quota requests); staying on gpt-4.1-mini.

key_decisions.choice: Legacy sites: gateway.call()/reserve()/settle() in the caller's transaction with the caller's estimate, reserving calls then tokens and releasing calls if tokens are refused (no savepoint, no session access by the gateway). Agent runs: begin_run() reserves the whole budget (model_calls=max_steps+1, tokens=max_total_tokens) and inserts agent_runs(status=running, lease) in its own committed transaction; provider calls run with no transaction open; finish_run() does feature writes, settle and audit in one transaction.
key_decisions.why: Keeps pinned numbers and stubbed-usage tests; satisfies 'reserved before it runs' for every agent step with one reservation and no row lock across agent calls; survives crashes without replay.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Per-step reservations with call ids (more round trips; only needed for checkpoint resume, which is not used); holding the advisory lock across a multi-call run.

key_decisions.choice: Settle from what the adapter reports: completed requests and their billed tokens are committed; each request that may have been processed (timeout, 5xx, transport error after send, malformed reply; plain ProviderError counts as one) commits one call and the per-call estimate; when nothing may have been processed (exception before any call, connect refused, token acquisition failure, HTTP 401/403/404/410/429) the reservation is released. Success commits billed tokens over all attempts and attempts as calls.
key_decisions.why: Replaces three behaviours across eleven sites; fixes connection-refused being charged at commit-estimate sites, repair attempts billed but not counted, and the uncharged compose_reply failure.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Per-site policies; always release (under-counts paid timeouts); always commit (charges when Ollama is simply down); changing router status codes here (pinned 503/502 assertions; left to P8).

key_decisions.decision: How pipelines are metered and how the rule is enforced
key_decisions.choice: Services pass gateway.metered(providers.chat) into run_turn; the proxy forwards complete/complete_once/respond/stream to the instance and records attempts, usage and failures. tests/test_architecture.py asserts that usage.reserve for model_calls or tokens appears only in domains/llm/gateway.py.
key_decisions.why: Pinned tests call run_turn directly with fakes and patch instance methods, so pipelines must keep calling the object they are handed. Every paid chat call needs a reservation, so bounding reservation sites to the gateway enforces one policy without forbidding chat calls in pipelines.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: AST guard on chat method calls (breaks pinned tests); passing session and gateway into the workflow functions (changes pinned signatures).

key_decisions.decision: Tools: what the model may touch
key_decisions.choice: Eager compact context plus lazy READ tools wrapping existing functions in their own short SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY session, learner_id injected from ToolContext, argument models with extra='forbid' and no identity field, results capped at 4000 characters. PROPOSE tools never write: they validate and stash a normalised proposal and return {accepted, errors:[codes]}; code applies accepted proposals in finish_run or on a learner click.
key_decisions.why: Keeps 'models propose, code decides' literal, makes cross-learner access structurally impossible and keeps most runs at one or two calls. stories.service.today_episode and stories.service.library are deliberately not tools (they lock, insert and can enqueue a paid job).
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Generic SQL or row tools; write tools with approval; tool-only design without eager context.

key_decisions.decision: Streaming transport and what may be streamed
key_decisions.choice: SSE over POST fetch on twin '.../stream' routes: sync generator routes returning fastapi.sse.EventSourceResponse that only drain a queue; an AgentRunner thread owns the run and settles in its own finally. Refusals happen in a dependency and stay JSON. Only the tutor's explanation_nl is streamed, sentence by sentence after a per-sentence gate; the final payload is authoritative and a replace event swaps in the fallback. Partner replies and all structured fields are sent only after validation. No mid-stream resume: a finished request_id replays one result event.
key_decisions.why: EventSource cannot POST or set X-Requested-With; the stack is sync; settlement must not depend on generator cleanup; unvalidated partner lines or keys on screen would break 'code validates everything'.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Accept negotiation on one route; generator-owned settlement; async routes with an async provider client; WebSocket; token-streaming everything; a replay buffer for 3-6 s replies.

key_decisions.choice: Free first: when the subject already has an explanation (authored question explanation released after submission, stored writing-correction explanation, feedback point note) the first tutor message is that text with no model call. The model runs for subjects without one, for why-follow-ups (cap 3) and to propose category, drill and words. One thread per (learner, subject_hash) is the cache. The drill is created only when the learner clicks.
key_decisions.why: Most 'Leg uit' taps cost nothing and always have a deterministic fallback; the agent adds value where the owner asked.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Always generate; cross-learner explanation cache; creating drill sessions inside the run (orphans).

key_decisions.decision: Study guide: trigger and who writes the reasons
key_decisions.choice: The web POSTs /today/guide once per Brussels day after Today has rendered (request id guide-<day>), plus two manual refreshes; no model run when the learner has no history. The model selects 3-5 ids from code-built candidates, orders them and assigns reason codes; code pins mandatory steps, checks each code against snapshot facts and renders trilingual reasons from templates with SQL numbers. An optional Dutch focus sentence must pass a deny-list and may contain only digits present in the snapshot.
key_decisions.why: Plain-language factual reasons without letting a model assert things about the learner; GET /today stays free and instant.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Free-text reasons; running inside GET /today; a job-loop run with polling (60 s lease, more moving parts); keeping reorder-3.

key_decisions.decision: Generative partner reply and its languages
key_decisions.choice: PARTNER_REPLY_MODE=reaction: after the unchanged interpretation call, one more single request writes a Dutch reaction of at most 120 characters with no question mark; code appends the authored anchor (cue, accepted plus next cue, success, hint). English/Persian show the authored anchor only. Guard: question marks, invalid-choice aliases, numbers/weekdays/times/prices absent from scenario copy and learner text, confirmation words when the goal was not accepted, non-Dutch or meta text, stage-vocabulary coverage. Rejection or failure gives the authored reply; the turn never fails on call two.
key_decisions.why: Facts and the next question always come from authored text, so the guard polices one sentence; Persian stays authored; cost stays near 0.8k tokens.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Fully free reply; trilingual generated reaction (unverifiable Persian, more tokens); authored only. A later 'paraphrase' mode is gated on the reply_guard eval suite and not built here.

key_decisions.choice: Table conversation_scenarios (validated Blueprint JSONB, validator report, status). Authored content/conversations/*.json stays static. Admin batches: generate, validate, review queue, publish. On-demand requests (3 a day) become visible to the requester once code validation passes, labelled generated and unreviewed, and enter the queue. dlp.cli export-scenarios can promote published rows to content/conversations/generated-<stage>.json.
key_decisions.why: The container must not write lesson files; mirrors D-18 (validated generated stories are shown unreviewed with a label); export gives version control when wanted.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Writing JSON at runtime; fully improvised scenarios with no stored blueprint; zero-call template scenarios from topic bundles (weaker goal validation; possible later).

key_decisions.decision: How tests script tool calls and streams
key_decisions.choice: chat_replies.json entry {'script':[{'tool_calls':[{'name':..,'arguments':{..}}]},...,{'final':{..},'chunks':[..]}]} chosen by prompt_version and indexed by the number of assistant tool-call turns already in messages (stateless). Placeholders $last and $tool.<name>.<path>; fail_after_chunks for broken streams; pytest may inject a callable. Fixture-produced judgements never become mistakes or assessed outcomes.
key_decisions.why: Deterministic multi-step runs with no hidden state between Playwright tests.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Call counters on the fixture instance; recorded cassettes.

key_decisions.choice: Bicep defaults: dailyModelCalls 250, dailyTokens 300000, totalModelCalls 40000, totalTokens 40000000 (about a twelve-month envelope), capacity 50 (small) and 30 (strong) subject to quota. Code budgets in domains/llm/budgets.py: tutor 3 steps/3500 tokens/30 s, follow-up 2/2500/20 s, guide 4/7000/30 s (3 runs a day), partner reaction 1 call/900, feedback 1 call/2500 (20 a day), scenario 2 calls/12000 (3 a day on demand, 10 a day admin), tutor threads 30 a day.
key_decisions.why: Typical day is about 90-95k tokens and 75-80 calls; heavy about 150k and 120; whole-run reservations need headroom; capacity 1 is 1K TPM, below one agent step.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Keeping 80/80k; removing caps for the owner. Prices were not verified: check the Azure calculator before approving.

key_decisions.choice: Settings and Bicep parameters, all off by default, exposed through GET /me features: AGENT_TUTOR_ENABLED, AGENT_STUDY_GUIDE_ENABLED, PARTNER_REPLY_MODE (off|reaction), CONVERSATION_FEEDBACK_ENABLED, SCENARIO_GENERATION_ENABLED, AGENT_STREAMING_ENABLED; plus AZURE_CHAT_API and AZURE_CHAT_PROFILE_SMALL/STRONG. Order: gateway, policy, LangGraph removal, port v2, Responses adapter on the existing deployment, runtime, tools, evals, new deployments and cutover, SSE, then in production tutor, feedback, reaction replies on the ten pilots, study guide, scenarios.
key_decisions.why: Each step is reviewable and reversible by an environment variable; the lowest-risk, highest-value feature ships first.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Switching adapter, model and agents together.

api.request: Headers X-Requested-With: fetch. Body {request_id: 8-80 [a-zA-Z0-9_-], subject: {kind: 'exercise_item'|'writing_correction'|'comprehension_question'|'conversation_feedback', ref: {session_id,item_id} | {review_id,index} | {stage_id,topic_id,skill,question_id} | {episode_id,question_index} | {conversation_id,point_index}}}, extra=forbid.
api.response: 200 {id, subject:{kind,title{nl,en,fa}}, status:'open', turns_left:3, messages:[{id, seq, role:'tutor', source:'authored'|'model'|'fallback'|'fixture', explanation:{nl, support, support_lang}, learner_quote, correct_form, category, recurring:bool, follow_ups:[str], drill:{available:bool}, word_suggestions:[{library_id,term}], review_status}]}. Stream twin events: run {run_id}, status {phase, tool}, delta {field:'explanation_nl', text} (whole gated sentences), replace {field, text}, result {same JSON}, error {code, retryable}, done {status}; id '<run_id>:<seq>'.
api.notes: Idempotent per request_id and per subject hash (re-opening returns the stored thread, no call). 409 item not submitted yet; 422 final-check subject; 404 not the owner; 403 when Azure paid use is off and no authored explanation exists; 429 allowance or daily cap. Opening an explanation earns no points. Flag AGENT_TUTOR_ENABLED. Disconnect on the stream cancels the run.

api.response: 200 thread view with the appended learner and tutor messages; tutor content {answer:{nl, support}, on_topic:bool, follow_ups[]}. Stream twin as above.
api.notes: Follow-up cap 3 per thread enforced in code (409 afterwards). Off-topic questions get a fixed authored line. Budget 2 steps / 2500 tokens / 20 s. Never a silent re-run: an interrupted request_id returns the stored fallback.

api.response: GET thread view. POST 201 {exercise_session_id, href}.

open_risks: Protocol ownership: Responses item types, SSE event names, the encrypted-reasoning echo and reasoning.context are maintained by us. Mitigation: ignore unknown items and events, contract tests on recorded payloads, AZURE_CHAT_API=chat_completions rollback while gpt-4.1-mini exists (until 2027-04-14), and the option to swap the adapter internals to the openai SDK without touching domain code.

No framework conveniences: no session memory abstraction, checkpoint/resume, human-in-the-loop, multi-agent or MCP. If the product needs them, Tool and AgentSpec port 1:1 to Agent Framework function tools; only the loop is discarded.

Local development quality: llama3.1:8b tool calling is unreliable and Ollama ignores tool_choice, so local agent runs often end in the deterministic fallback. Agents are verified on scripted fixtures in CI and on Azure by the eval run, not on the laptop model.

Model facts that the sources leave open: the gpt-5.6 version string (2026-07-09 versus 2026-06-25), whether gpt-6 accepts temperature, whether a classic model accepts a Responses request as the adapter builds it, quota for gpt-5.6 on this subscription, and prices. All are settled by the Models API, one chat-probe call and the Azure calculator before cutover; none was verified here.

Losing temperature on reasoning models may change interpretation consistency and removes the story writer's 0.7 diversity knob. Effort none plus strict schemas should compensate for interpretation; story variety must come from prompt inputs. Do not cut over without the Azure eval run and a look at three generated episodes.

Data Zone Standard processes anywhere in the EU, not only West Europe; GO_LIVE currently promises regional processing. The owner should accept this explicitly in the new DECISIONS entry; the only regional alternative retires on 2027-04-14.

The SSE path is unproven in production: Next compression, the Easy Auth sidecar and Container Apps ingress could buffer or cut idle streams, and the BaseHTTPMiddleware in main.py may mask disconnects under starlette 1.6.0. Every streaming endpoint has a JSON twin, the web helper falls back to it, and AGENT_STREAMING_ENABLED can stay off.

Sync execution model: one thread per run plus the request thread draining its queue, cooperative cancellation only, and a streamed call holds a slot of the per-model semaphore (max_concurrent_model_calls=2) while the in-process job loop may want it. Acceptable for one learner on a 0.25 vCPU replica; a ceiling for many.

Validators are heuristics (substring grounding, deny-lists, vocabulary coverage, number and name extraction). They can reject good output (higher fallback rate) and cannot prove that a Dutch explanation, a better form or a reaction is correct or natural. Outputs stay labelled generated/unreviewed; measure fallback and rejection rates from agent_runs and review about 50 live outputs per feature before widening a flag.

A confidently wrong grammar explanation is the main pedagogical risk of the tutor; hence the strong tier, the follow-up cap, grounding on authored category notes and the eval gate. Generated Persian in tutor explanations is checked for script and length only.

The failure-policy change is visible to the learner: missions, writing and rubric feedback used to refund allowance on any failure and now keep a conservative charge after timeouts. Together with whole-run reservations a learner near the daily cap is refused earlier, so caps must be raised before the first flag is enabled.

The study guide makes one automatic paid run per day on the first Today visit. It is bounded and switchable but departs from 'page views are free'; the owner should confirm this rather than an explicit button (the fallback is to trigger it only from 'Stel samen').
The 'total' usage scope is a lifetime counter; 40 M tokens is about a year of typical use. Either the owner raises it at each model migration or a monthly scope is added by the platform track.

Platform issues outside this track still bite: the 60 s job lease with no heartbeat (scenario generation uses a 45 s call timeout and max_attempts=1), usage_counters row locks held across provider calls at legacy in-transaction sites, and the conversation row lock now spanning two calls. Mutual exclusion between a legacy call and an agent run can overlap for one request if the legacy call starts just before begin_run commits.

Cross-track coupling: learner profile and GET /me features (P2), record_activity and the Today planner (P3), the exercise generator and learner_mistakes (P4), components/ui primitives, the exercise kit, TanStack Query and the UI-copy catalogue (web). Tools and snapshot sections degrade to empty when a seam is missing; S12 and S14 wait for the web seams. TodayHome.tsx and TopicConversation.tsx are edited by more than one track; migration and DECISIONS numbers are assigned at merge.

Stateless tool loops resend the growing input (tool results plus encrypted reasoning items) each step; with effort low and four steps the study guide can approach its 7000-token ceiling. The ceiling stops the run and the planner fallback is shown, so the failure mode is cost-bounded but visible.

Default Azure content filters are not tuned for Dutch; a content_filter refusal is mapped to a friendly message and the authored fallback, but false blocks on harmless Dutch are possible and not controllable from code.

design.approach_summary:
All paths are relative to ROOT = C:/Users/Nima/Desktop/MINE/My_projects/Dutch Learning Platform/Final_Project_v1.

Build one server-owned exercise engine (apps/api/src/dlp/domains/exercises) that turns the existing library words, topic bundles, lesson and grammar content into short mixed sessions. A session is generated once from a seed and stored with a private key per item. The browser receives prompts only, sends one answer at a time, and gets back the outcome, the correct answer, the glosses and a token diff. Missed items return once at the end. Code computes the summary, awards points through record_activity, writes learner_mistakes rows and proposes missed words for the word bank.

Topic and lesson completion do not change: only first-attempt answers to the authored questions count, through the existing objective_result and the persistence extracted from save_topic_practice. Open speaking and writing still complete only through the model rubric. Final-check content is never a source.

On the web, one runner (components/exercise/ExerciseSession.tsx, a reducer state machine) with a renderer registry replaces the five multiple-choice renderers, VocabularyRecall, the alphabet quiz and WordReview. Sessions appear as the Today warm-up, the default Start of every topic, the path lesson, word review and a while-you-wait activity.

Order: safety tests, activity slice, comparison and read-aloud, engine API in three slices, web kit in two, then one surface at a time with its e2e rewrite. Model-judged kinds, the verb bank and generated items follow the agent platform.

Critical files (under ROOT): apps/api/src/dlp/domains/curriculum/topics.py; apps/api/src/dlp/domains/stories/validator.py; apps/api/src/dlp/domains/speech/service.py; apps/web/components/SkillTopicPractice.tsx; apps/web/components/CurriculumControls.tsx.

key_decisions.decision: Where items are generated and graded
key_decisions.choice: The server materialises every session: exercise_items stores the public prompt and a private key per item. The browser gets prompts only and makes one round trip per answer (POST .../answer).
key_decisions.why: The rule is 'code decides; keys never sent before an answer'. Points, mistake rows and topic completion need outcomes the server can trust, and the tutor agent can later propose drills that pass through the same generators and validators.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Client-side generation from GET /library/{stage}/vocabulary (the review's suggestion): keys are public and nothing is evidence. A stateless per-item check endpoint: no retry queue, no idempotent points. Hashed keys in the payload: 2-4 options are brute-forceable and tolerant typed grading is impossible.

key_decisions.choice: seed = first 8 bytes of sha256(learner_id:request_id:GENERATOR_VERSION 'ex-v1'); one random.Random drives item selection, distractors and order. Items are persisted at creation. exercise_sessions has UNIQUE(learner_id, request_id); the same id with different parameters returns 409 (reuse coaching.service.fingerprint). Answer request ids are stored in the item's attempts under a row lock and replay the stored response. Finish returns the stored summary. Points use request ids exi-<item id> and exs-<session id> in record_activity. Tiles and sentence orders are never served in solved order.
key_decisions.why: A retried POST must not create a second session or award twice, and a content rebuild or generator change must not alter a session in progress.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Seeding from date and topic only (a retry gives the identical session). Regenerating from the seed on every read (breaks when content JSON changes; depends on Python's shuffle implementation).

key_decisions.choice: Only first-attempt answers to the authored questions count. On finish the service maps the chosen option ids back to original indices and calls the unchanged curriculum.service.objective_result (75%, so both of two), then _persist_topic_result (extracted from topics.save_topic_practice lines 243-273): sticky TopicPractice.completed, CurriculumPractice, PracticeObservation with source 'topic_practice' and request id ex-<session id>. Derived items earn points only. Speaking and writing sessions are scaffolds; completion there still comes only from POST /curriculum/{stage}/topics/{topic}/practice.
key_decisions.why: Keeps docs/TOPIC_PRACTICE.md and the test_topics.py pins. Unreviewed generated items must not gate the final-check prerequisite. A retry after seeing the key cannot become a pass within the same session.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Completion at 75% of all session items (changes documented meaning). Completion on finishing a session (equivalent to a self-report). Deleting the classic practice endpoint now (API tests and productive flow depend on it).

key_decisions.decision: Final-check withholding and practice key leaks
key_decisions.choice: Generators read only topics_for(), library_for(), stage.lesson, stage.grammar and stage.vocabulary; never stage.test. A test asserts no prompt or key contains a stage.test question id or sentence (measured today: zero shared texts or sentences in all 12 stages). public_test and attempt_view are untouched. Once grammar, the lesson and Story Time run on the engine, stage_view and story_detail stop sending answer_index and explanations; Story Time checks through POST /library/{stage}/stories/{id}/answer.
key_decisions.why: Reading questions at six stages are identical to Story Time questions that ship with their key, so hiding keys only in the engine would hide nothing.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Leaving practice keys in stage view (docs/CURRICULUM.md allows it today): contradicts 'keys never sent before an answer' and lets a key be read from the network tab.

key_decisions.choice: At most two attempts per item. A first-attempt wrong, almost or skipped item is asked once more at the end, with options or tiles reshuffled by (seed, position, attempt). The queue is derived from item states on the server, so a reload resumes exactly. Nothing blocks finishing; there are no hearts or lives.
key_decisions.why: Non-punitive by decision; server-derived state makes resume and two-tab use safe without extra columns.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: A client-owned queue (lost on reload). Unlimited retries until correct (turns into copying the revealed answer).

key_decisions.choice: 1 point when an item closes (the same for right and wrong), 2 for a shadow attempt that was heard, 5 for finishing a session of at least 5 items. Word-review items keep their existing single point from vocab.review and award nothing extra. All through record_activity with a skill tag.
key_decisions.why: D-19 as revised: reward doing, never judge Dutch. A 10-item session gives 15 of the 20-point daily goal.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Points only for correct answers (judges Dutch). A daily cap (not needed for one learner; noted as a risk because word review is already uncapped).

key_decisions.choice: A learner_mistakes row is written on a first-attempt wrong or almost, with a category derived from kind and diff: vocabulary_meaning, vocabulary_form, article, spelling, word_order, grammar_form, missing_word, listening_discrimination, comprehension. A taxonomy_version column records the rule set. The row is resolved when the same ref is answered correctly first time in a later session. None for shadow, allowance skips or overridden answers.
key_decisions.why: Gives the warm-up, the 'herhaal je fouten' session, the learner snapshot and the tutor's memory of recurring error types one factual source.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Reusing practice_observations.failed_refs (topic-only, no category, no learner text). Letting a model classify errors (paid, not reproducible).

key_decisions.decision: Word bank: suggest, do not auto-enrol
key_decisions.choice: Missed library words become word_suggestions rows (one per lemma, with miss_count). The summary offers 'Bewaar alle' and per-word 'Bewaar' (POST /words with source_kind 'library', source_id = library word id); /woorden lists open suggestions with dismiss.
key_decisions.why: Missed items come back anyway through the warm-up and mistakes sessions. Auto-enrolment would inflate the due count, which reads as punishment, and it would break D-19's 'the learner's own choice'.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Auto-saving every missed word. Deriving suggestions on each read from learner_mistakes (cannot be dismissed).

key_decisions.decision: Speech allowance and caching for audio items
key_decisions.choice: New speech.service.synthesize_cached(): blob key tts-cache/<provider>/<voice>/<sha256 of text>.wav. A hit returns the stored bytes with no reservation; a miss runs the existing synthesize_text (reserve, call, settle) and stores the result. Only static course text is cached, never learner text. Item audio is served by POST /exercises/sessions/{id}/items/{item_id}/audio because the text is the answer. When creating a session the blueprint reads usage.snapshot() (not usage.remaining(), which returns 0 when no counter row exists) and replaces audio kinds if the daily audio_seconds left is below the estimate. The audio route and the shadow transcription never hold the item row lock during a provider call.
key_decisions.why: Production allows 1,200 audio seconds a day shared by speech-to-text and text-to-speech; replays and repeated sessions must not spend it.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Calling speech/synthesize from the browser with the text (reveals dictation and listen-and-choose answers). Browser-only cache (32 clips per tab, lost on reload).

key_decisions.choice: The API returns structured results (outcome, expected answer, diff ops, category, content-derived Localized explanations and translations). The web builds the sentences from the typed UI-copy catalogue, so instructions and feedback follow the Dutch-plus-gloss rule in one place.
key_decisions.why: Avoids trilingual string building in Python and keeps chrome copy in the shared catalogue.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Server-built nl/en/fa feedback strings as objective_result does today.

key_decisions.choice: components/exercise/sessionReducer.ts is a pure reducer. States: idle, creating, answering, checking, feedback, finishing, summary, plus error and exit-confirm overlays. Events: CREATED, RESUMED, DRAFT_CHANGED, SUBMIT, ANSWERED, ANSWER_FAILED, SKIP, CONTINUE, FINISHED, EXIT. A request id is minted once per (item, attempt) and reused on network retry (the submitKey pattern in SkillTopicPractice.tsx). ExerciseSession.tsx runs effects, registry.ts maps kind to renderer. It runs full page at /oefenen (focus mode without the mobile tab bar) or embedded in a topic, /woorden and the Today pending card.
key_decisions.why: A reducer is unit-testable with the existing node --experimental-strip-types runner and keeps the runner independent of the data library. Server responses are events, not cache entries.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Holding session state in TanStack Query cache (answers are commands, not queries; Query is used only for suggestions, mistakes and invalidating Today after finish). One component per surface, as today.

key_decisions.decision: Keyboard, screen reader, touch and motion
key_decisions.choice: Choice items are real radio inputs in a fieldset styled as cards. Keys: 1-4 select, Enter checks or continues, Esc opens the exit dialog, D/H for de/het, Space hold-to-talk via talkButtonHandlers. Tiles and ordering use tap-to-place and Omhoog/Omlaag buttons. On a new item focus moves to its heading after commit; on feedback focus moves to 'Verder'; a polite live region announces the outcome and each pair result. Outcome is shown by icon and text as well as colour. Targets are at least 44 px; options stack at 320 px. Animations exist only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
key_decisions.why: The axe gate requires zero violations at 1440, 390 and 320 px; the repo already moves focus after commit rather than on an animation frame.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: A drag-and-drop library (new dependency, weak keyboard support). Custom div buttons for options (loses native radio semantics and the input[name=...] selectors).

key_decisions.decision: Migrating the five multiple-choice renderers and the three small tools
key_decisions.choice: A presentational components/exercise/ChoiceGroup.tsx becomes the only option renderer. CurriculumQuestions, QuestionList, EpisodeReader.Questions, VideoPlayer.Questions and CurriculumTest (exam mode) become thin adapters that keep their class names and radio names. VocabularyRecall is deleted and WordLibrary starts a words session. The AlphabetPractice quiz becomes a listen_choose session; the letter chart stays. WordReview runs source word_review.
key_decisions.why: Existing e2e specs prove the adapters behave the same; a new item kind is then added in one place.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Rewriting all five surfaces onto server sessions at once (stories and videos grade a batch once by design; the final check must stay a single submission).

key_decisions.choice: Dutch options are sent as {nl} only; en/fa glosses arrive in the answer response. Passage translations and listening transcripts unlock after the comprehension items close. Option order is shuffled per attempt. Vocabulary questions have 4 options. The legacy CurriculumQuestions hides option glosses until checked.
key_decisions.why: Today the English gloss under each option answers 100 of 400 questions per beginner stage, and two fixed options pass by chance 25% of the time.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Adding invented distractors to every authored comprehension question: a borrowed option can be true for the text and cannot be checked deterministically. Those questions keep their authored 2-3 options until reviewed generated distractors exist.

key_decisions.choice: topic+reading (9-10 items): match_pairs on the 5 topic words, listen_choose or choice, read_passage, the 2 authored questions, cloze_choice from the text, sentence_order (a2 and above) or sentence_builder, typed_recall, dictation. topic+listening: match_pairs, 2 listen_choose, listen_passage (existing /listening endpoint), the 2 authored questions, dictation of one text sentence, cloze_choice. topic+speaking scaffold: listen_choose, sentence_builder and 2 shadow items from speaking.sample, then the open task. topic+writing scaffold: 2 typed_recall, cloze_typed on writing.sample, sentence_builder, dictation, then the open task. stage_skill: the same with stage.lesson, or focus words, grammar or alphabet. word_review: up to 20 due vocab_items. warmup: 5-6 items from open mistakes, due words and the next topic. mistakes: 8 missed refs asked with a different kind. while_you_wait: 5 tap-only items, no typing, no model.
key_decisions.why: Follows the loop in docs/LEARNING_DESIGN.md (preview words, recall, read or listen, then produce) using only existing fields.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: One fixed recipe for all stages (sentence ordering needs 3+ sentences, absent before a2; de/het is useless from c1; odd-one-out is ambiguous once topics hold 25-100 words).

key_decisions.choice: At load, fingerprint each topic's reading and listening text. Topic list and detail gain review_of {stage_id, topic_id} when an earlier stage has the same text; the UI shows 'Herhaling van pre-A1' and, if the earlier twin is completed, runs a shorter session with production kinds instead of recognition. Story Time hides stories whose text equals a topic reading (100 of 100 at most stages, 50 at pre-c2 and c2) and the section disappears when fewer than five remain, linking to /verhalen. WordLibrary says so when a stage reuses an earlier word list. Each session uses at most one item per sentence frame.
key_decisions.why: Only 399 unique titles fill 1,200 topic slots; drills tolerate reuse when it is labelled as review, but pretending it is new makes progress feel like repetition.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Deleting duplicate content (the schema requires 100 topics and 100 stories per stage, and tests pin it). Leaving Story Time as a second copy of the reading texts.

key_decisions.decision: Later: generated items, verb bank and conjugation
key_decisions.choice: A job asks the model for items or verb forms for one stage and topic. exercises/validator.py gates them: schema; Dutch only; stage vocabulary coverage via stories.validator.coverage; exactly one key, grounded by a quote from the source; distractors absent from the source; alternates that are pure permutations; regular verb forms cross-checked by a rule engine. Rows land in generated_items. Mechanical kinds may be served once validated; comprehension items and irregular verbs also need owner approval in the content-review queue. Served items are labelled generated and unreviewed and have a report button.
key_decisions.why: Models propose, code decides; a validator cannot prove that a comprehension distractor is false, so those wait for a human.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Serving generated comprehension items after automatic checks only. Promising conjugation drills before a checked verb table exists.

key_decisions.decision: Kind: choice (word meaning and authored comprehension)
key_decisions.choice: Feeds: LibraryWord.term, meaning{nl,en,fa}, topic; authored Question prompt, options, answer_index, explanation from topic reading/listening, lesson and grammar practice. Generator: the word variant picks a direction by seed, then the correct option plus 3 distractors with the same LibraryWord.topic.nl, a different lemma_key and a different normalised meaning in all three languages, filled from neighbouring topics if needed. The authored variant shuffles the authored options; 'Wat betekent X' questions whose correct option equals a library meaning.nl get 2 same-topic meaning distractors. Options get opaque ids after shuffling. Grader: option id equals key. Feedback: correct option marked, the explanation, example sentence with audio, glosses of all options.
key_decisions.why: Removes fixed positions and the gloss giveaway while using only authored material.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Grading by option index (breaks once options are shuffled).

key_decisions.choice: Feeds: 4-5 LibraryWords (topic.vocabulary_ids or one library topic): term and meaning.en/fa, or meaning.nl when the support meaning exceeds 40 characters. Generator: words with pairwise different lemma_key and meanings; right column shuffled. Grader: each tapped pair is a partial answer {left,right} checked by id; the item closes when all pairs are matched; first-attempt outcome is correct with no wrong pair, almost with one, otherwise wrong. Each missed word becomes its own retry item and mistake row. Feedback: the pair locks with a check icon or is released with 'Nog niet'; on close every term has an audio button.
key_decisions.why: Instant per-pair feedback is the point of the mechanic; the protocol also accepts all pairs in one answer if latency proves too high.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Checking pairs in the browser (needs the key).

key_decisions.choice: Feeds: LibraryWord.example.nl with the term blanked; topic reading sentences containing a topic word. Generator: pool.find_term_span() finds the core term (stories.validator.lemma_key) as a whole-word, case-insensitive match. Cards where the surface form differs from the core term, occurs twice or is not contiguous are skipped for this kind, so every option is a bare lemma. Distractors are 3 same-topic terms of the same article class. Grader: option id. Feedback: the full sentence with the word highlighted, example.en/fa, audio.
key_decisions.why: An inflected correct option among lemma distractors would give the answer away.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: A plain substring search (false hits such as 'kort' in 'kortere'; 113 of 6,000 cards have no match at all).

key_decisions.decision: Kind: cloze_typed, and the tolerant comparison used by all typed kinds
key_decisions.choice: Feeds: the same sentences, inflected forms allowed; a hint (first letter and length) marks the item assisted. compare.compare_text: (1) NFKC, casefold, trim punctuation and quotes, collapse spaces; (2) equal is correct; (3) missing article is correct, wrong article is almost with category article; (4) equal after removing diacritics is correct with an accent note; (5) Damerau-Levenshtein distance up to 1 for 4-7 letters and up to 2 for 8 or more is almost with category spelling, never for 3 letters or fewer and never when the typed word is another library term; the lemma typed where an inflected form is needed is almost with category grammar_form; otherwise wrong. Feedback: expected word, character diff, sentence audio, translation, and 'Mijn antwoord was ook goed'.
key_decisions.why: Typos and accents should read as 'almost', not as failure, without accepting a different real word.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Exact match (too harsh). Unlimited fuzzy match (accepts 'bus' for 'bos').

key_decisions.choice: Feeds: LibraryWord.term spoken by text-to-speech with the text withheld; options are 4 written same-topic terms or 4 meanings. At pre-a1 also the 26 letter names from a server table exercises/alphabet.py that mirrors apps/web/lib/alphabet.ts. Grader: option id. Feedback: the written term, its meaning, replay; category listening_discrimination.
key_decisions.why: Generalises the only existing instant-feedback mechanic (AlphabetPractice) to every stage.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Keeping the quiz in the browser with letterQuestion() (no points, fixed order).

key_decisions.choice: Feeds: a single term at pre-a1, otherwise a sentence of 3-12 tokens without digits or abbreviations from LibraryWord.example.nl, topic listening text split by stories.validator.sentences, or grammar examples. Audio only. Grader: both sides tokenised by stories.validator.tokens after folding, diacritics ignored; a longest-common-subsequence alignment yields ops equal, replace, insert, delete. Correct when all are equal; almost when at most 20% of tokens differ and each difference is a near-miss spelling or one missing or extra function word; otherwise wrong. Feedback: the expected sentence with per-token marks (TokenDiff), translation, replay.
key_decisions.why: A token diff shows exactly which word was missed, which is the learning moment.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Whole-string comparison (one typo fails the sentence with no explanation).

key_decisions.decision: Kind: typed_recall, and its SM-2 mapping in word review
key_decisions.choice: Feeds: LibraryWord.meaning in the support language as cue and term as answer; in word review VocabItem.meaning_en/meaning_fa and term (a flashcard with self-grade is used when a saved word has no meaning). Grader: compare_text with variants {term, term without article}. Feedback: the term with its article, example with audio, override button. Mapping, applied once through vocab.review with request id ex-<item id>: correct without hint is good; correct with hint or accent note, or almost, is hard; wrong or skipped is again; easy only when the learner taps 'Te makkelijk'.
key_decisions.why: Recall is finally checked, and review grades come from evidence rather than self-rating.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Inferring 'easy' from response time (unreliable on phones). Keeping pure self-rating.

key_decisions.choice: Feeds: LibraryWord.term starting with de or het (220/89 at pre-a1, 344/57 at pre-b2). Disabled from c1, where 98% are de. Generator: 6 nouns per item, het-words sampled at 50%, shown without article. Grader: one partial answer per noun {word, bin}, exact. Feedback: the full form such as 'het huis' with audio; category article with the lemma.
key_decisions.why: Balanced sampling stops 'always de' from scoring 70%.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Rule explanations for plurals and diminutives (no authored data).

key_decisions.choice: Feeds: sentences of 3-9 tokens from LibraryWord.example.nl (355 at pre-a1, 153 at a1, 500 at a2, 359 at pre-b2), grammar examples and speaking/writing sample sentences; elsewhere 10-20-token sentences cut into 4-6 chunks at commas and conjunctions. Cue: example.en/fa. Generator: tiles shuffled; a sentence-initial capital is lowered when the word is a function word; final punctuation is fixed; sentences with movable time adverbs are avoided. Grader: the folded tile sequence equals the authored sequence, identical tokens interchangeable; otherwise wrong, with override 'Mijn zin kan ook'. Feedback: the authored sentence, the first differing position, audio; category word_order.
key_decisions.why: Dutch allows inversion, so a different order can be valid; the override keeps the grader honest and never affects completion.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Deriving accepted alternatives by rule (unsafe without parsing); reviewed alternates come with the generated-items pipeline.

key_decisions.choice: Feeds: 3-4 consecutive sentences of at most 160 characters from topic reading text, stages a2 and above (earlier texts have 2 sentences, so the blueprint substitutes sentence_builder). Shown after the passage, with the passage hidden. Grader: exact id order; one adjacent swap is almost. Feedback: the numbered correct order with translation; category comprehension.
key_decisions.why: Works best exactly where multiple-choice answers are sentences copied from the text (pre-b2 to pre-c1).
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Ordering two paragraphs at beginner stages (a coin flip).

key_decisions.choice: Feeds: 3 terms from one library topic and 1 from a topic at least 10 positions away, stages pre-a1 to b1. The prompt names the situation ('Welk woord hoort niet bij ...?'). Grader: option id. Feedback: names both topics; category vocabulary_meaning.
key_decisions.why: Beginner topics hold 5-10 tightly related words; from pre-b2 topics hold 25-100 and the odd word is no longer clear.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Using it at all stages.

key_decisions.choice: Feeds: a visible sentence of 3-10 tokens (examples, speaking.sample sentences, conversation step examples) with text-to-speech. Flow: listen, record with useRecorder, multipart answer; the server transcribes with keep_recording=False and runs speech.compare.read_aloud_compare. Outcome is only heard or not_heard. The response lists the transcript and matched and missed words. No percentage, pass mark, mistake row or retry-queue entry. Skipped automatically when the recorder, microphone or audio allowance is unavailable. Only this kind is tagged skill speaking.
key_decisions.why: D-20: a transcript cannot carry a pronunciation score; typed input never counts as speaking.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: A recognition threshold for 'correct' (a score by another name; it is also why read-aloud points are lost today below 50%).

key_decisions.decision: Later kinds: translate, error correction, conjugation
key_decisions.choice: translate: code tries exact and near match first; otherwise one LlmGateway call with a strict schema whose issue quotes must be substrings of the learner's sentence; code derives the outcome; when paid usage is off or the per-session budget of 3 is spent the item becomes compare-with-reference. error_correction: deterministic de/het swaps first, then personal items from stored writing corrections. conjugation: needs the checked verb table.
key_decisions.why: These need either a model judge or data that does not exist yet (the banks hold infinitives but no conjugated forms).
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Shipping them in the first release with strict string comparison.

api.request: {request_id: 8-80 chars [a-zA-Z0-9_-], source: 'topic'|'stage_skill'|'word_review'|'warmup'|'mistakes'|'while_you_wait', stage_id?, topic_id?, skill?: 'reading'|'listening'|'speaking'|'writing', focus?: 'words'|'grammar'|'alphabet', library_topic?: string, size?: 5-12, fresh?: bool}; extra fields forbidden.
api.response: 201 {id, source, stage_id, topic_id, skill, status, content_status: 'unreviewed', resumed: bool, audio_degraded: bool, items: [public item], progress: {closed, total, queued}}. 200 when replayed or resumed.
api.notes: Idempotent on (learner, request_id); the same id with other parameters returns 409. Unless fresh is true, an active session under 12 hours old for the same source, stage, topic and skill is returned; older ones are marked abandoned. No keys, no option glosses, no dictation text in the body. 404 unknown stage or topic; 422 invalid combination. No model call.

api.response: Same session view; closed items include their stored feedback; passage translations and listening transcript appear once the comprehension items are closed.
api.notes: Learner-scoped; another learner's id returns 404. Used for resume after reload.

api.request: JSON {request_id, answer, hint_used?: bool}. answer by kind: {option: 'b'}; {left, right}; {word, bin: 'de'|'het'}; {text: up to 300 chars}; {tiles: [ids]}; {order: [ids]}; {grade: 'again'|'hard'|'good'|'easy'} for flashcard and the optional 'Te makkelijk'; {done: true} for passages. Shadow sends multipart: request_id and audio.
api.response: {item_id, attempt, outcome: 'correct'|'almost'|'wrong'|'pair_correct'|'pair_wrong'|'heard'|'not_heard'|'done', closed, requeue, attempts_left, correct: {...}, explanation?: {nl,en,fa}, support?: {option glosses, translation}, diff?: [{op, expected, given}], category?, word?: {library_id, term, meaning, example, in_bank}, read_aloud?: {transcript, target_words, matched_words, missed, extra}, points, day: {points, target, met}, progress}
api.notes: The item row is locked for the write; a repeated request_id replays the stored response; a different answer under the same id returns 409; a closed item returns 409. For shadow the transcription runs before the lock; 429 allowance and 503 provider follow the existing mappers and leave the item open. The response never contains a score or percentage. First-attempt misses write learner_mistakes; closing awards points once.

api.response: Answer response with outcome 'skipped' and the correct answer.
api.notes: A learner skip is re-queued once; microphone or audio reasons close the item with no mistake row.

api.response: {item_id, outcome: 'self_accepted', closed: true, progress}
api.notes: Only for cloze_typed, typed_recall, sentence_builder and later translate, and only after a wrong or almost. Removes the mistake row, maps to SM-2 'hard' in word review, and never touches topic or stage completion.

api.response: audio/wav with headers X-Audio-Label, X-Audio-Voice, Cache-Control: no-store
api.notes: Speaks the item's withheld text through synthesize_cached; a cache hit reserves nothing. 404 for items without audio; 429 when the allowance is spent. Takes no row lock and creates no progress.

api.response: {status: 'finished', summary: {items_total, first_try_correct, fixed_on_retry, skipped, points_earned, by_kind, by_skill, missed: [{ref, expected}], suggestions: [word suggestion], topic?: {skill, completed, passed, correct, total}, next: {kind: 'open_task'|'next_topic'|'today', stage_id?, topic_id?}}, day: {points, target, met}}
api.notes: Idempotent; returns the stored summary when already finished. Requires all items closed unless early. For topic and lesson reading or listening it runs objective_result on first-attempt answers to the authored questions and persists completion as today. The session bonus is awarded once when at least 5 items were answered.

api.response: {items: [{id, category, kind, skill, stage_id, ref, lemma, expected, given, created_at, resolved_at}], by_category: {category: count}}
api.notes: Read-only and learner-scoped; also the data behind the snapshot's frequent mistake categories and the tutor's read tool.

api.response: GET {items: [{id, term, meaning_en, meaning_fa, example, source_id, miss_count, reason}]}; POST 204.
