verification: After every step: cd apps/api && ruff check src tests && pytest -q with TEST_DATABASE_URL set (PostgreSQL 16), then cd apps/web && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test:unit, then python scripts/run.py e2e with fixture providers. node_modules is absent in this worktree, so npm ci is needed first.

Migrations: alembic upgrade head from 0007 on a database with existing learning_days, vocab_items and topic_practice rows; downgrade one revision and upgrade again; python -m dlp.release still validates content before touching the database.

Key withholding: a test serialises every generated prompt for 200 seeds across the 12 stages and asserts the key text, option glosses and dictation sentences are absent; manually confirm in the browser network tab on a dictation and a listen-and-choose item.

Determinism and idempotency: the same create request twice returns byte-identical sessions; a double-clicked answer and two tabs answering the same item produce one attempt, one activity event and one mistake row.

Completion semantics: test_exercises_topic_completion.py shows first-try-correct authored questions complete the topic and stage skill, retry-correct does not, earlier completion stays, scaffold sessions and overrides never complete anything, and four completed skills still open the final check.
Final-check isolation: test_exercises_final_check_isolation.py plus the unchanged test_final_test_never_exposes_keys_samples_or_listening_transcript.

Speech allowance: a second audio request for the same item leaves usage counters unchanged; with the daily audio allowance at zero a session is created without audio kinds; shadow reserves audio seconds before transcription and stores no recording.
No pronunciation score: tests assert the strings 'score' and 'percent' are absent from shadow and /speech/read-aloud responses.

Accessibility gate: exercises.spec.ts runs axe (WCAG 2.1 A/AA) with zero violations at 1440, 390 and 320 px for every renderer in idle and feedback states, checks no horizontal overflow, completes a session with the keyboard only, and repeats with reduced motion emulated. One manual screen-reader pass (NVDA) through a full session.

Local run on Ollama: the engine makes no chat call, so a full session must work with CHAT_PROVIDER=local and the local Piper voice; confirm the Today warm-up, a topic session, word review and while-you-wait by hand.

Azure after release: extend scripts/verify_live.py with create, answer, finish on one pre-a1 words session; check GET /usage shows audio seconds only on first plays; confirm telemetry spans carry kind and outcome counts but no prompts, answers or identifiers.

Docs: docs/DECISIONS.md has the new numbered entries; LEARNING_DESIGN.md, TOPIC_PRACTICE.md, PRACTICE_LIBRARY.md, CURRICULUM.md, ENGINEERING.md and VERIFICATION.md describe the behaviour that the tests pin.
open_risks: Content quality: items are built from unreviewed and heavily templated sentences (a2, pre-b1 and b1 examples use 54-57 sentence frames). The one-item-per-frame rule and the availability matrix reduce repetition but cannot make awkward Dutch natural; a 'report this exercise' control arrives only with X16.

Authored comprehension questions keep 2 options at pre-a1 to b1, so passing a topic by guessing stays at about 25%. Shuffling and hidden glosses remove the giveaways, not the odds; proper third and fourth options need the reviewed generated-items pipeline.

Grader false negatives: valid alternative word orders and synonyms are marked wrong. The override keeps this honest and never affects completion, but if it is used often the sentence filters or thresholds need tuning.
The mistake taxonomy is heuristic. The tutor's 'recurring error types' will only be as good as these categories; taxonomy_version allows a later re-derivation, but old rows keep old labels.

Latency: every answer is a signed proxy call to a 0.25 vCPU single replica with synchronous routes. Match pairs and de/het send one call per tap. If p95 exceeds about 300 ms, switch those two kinds to whole-board submission, which the protocol already accepts.

Shadow items block a worker thread for the length of a transcription, like every existing speech route; several in a row on the small replica can delay other requests until the platform track moves provider calls out of request threads.

Audio allowance is shared between speech-to-text and text-to-speech (1,200 s a day in production). The cache removes replays, but a day of new topics with dictation plus voice work can still hit the cap; sessions then degrade to non-audio kinds.

End-to-end churn: five specs are rewritten (skill-topics, learning-tools, library-writing, curriculum, stories). Mocked specs can pass while the real API regresses; each surface therefore needs at least one unmocked case.

Shared seams: activity_events and migration numbers are touched by two tracks, and the Today layout by three. Agree owners and order before X02 and X12; record_activity needs skill and meta beyond the six named arguments.

Learner profile dependency: warm-up and while-you-wait need one stage. Until GET /me exists they take series.stage_id from the Today plan, which keeps the known mismatch (A1 stories, pre-A1 path) visible in practice.

The classic receptive practice endpoint stays reachable and still returns keys after any full submission, so sticky completion can be obtained outside the session flow by calling the API directly. Acceptable for one owner-learner; retire the receptive branch in P8.
learner_mistakes.given stores what the learner typed. It is covered by export and cascade deletion and kept out of telemetry, but it is new personal content in the database.
Automatic SM-2 grades can mis-schedule a word (a typo becomes 'hard'); word review also remains an uncapped source of points.
Hiding Story Time removes the section at ten of twelve stages. That is the intent, but it must ship together with the link to the generated serial or it reads as lost content.

Tables grow by about ten item rows per session with prompt and key JSON. No pruning is planned in P4; add a retention job (for example abandoned sessions after 30 days) with the structural hardening phase.

design.track: Learner journey — profile, onboarding, one level, gloss layer, navigation, Today session, points for all practice, progress dashboard, waiting/empty states, copy (P2 and P3)
design.approach_summary: One server-side learner profile (new `learner_profiles` table, migration 0008, GET/PATCH /me, POST /me/onboarding) becomes the only source for level, daily goal and support mode; the story series, coach, videos and path all read it. The web keeps localStorage as a synchronous cache and syncs it with the server. First run is detected client-side (`FirstRunGate` on `onboarded_at`) and redirected to a bare-shell `/welkom` flow; the first episode is pre-queued by the onboarding POST while GET /today keeps its test-pinned behaviour. A typed copy catalogue plus `UiText` puts English/Persian glosses under Dutch chrome and fades them by stage; e2e runs with glosses off through a per-test profile-reset fixture so existing selectors survive. Navigation shrinks to five tabs (Vandaag, Leren, Verhalen, Spreken, Woorden) with Voortgang and Instellingen in the sidebar and header. In P3 an `activity` domain (`record_activity`, append-only `activity_events`, migration 0009) replaces direct `add_points`, awards fixed effort points for every server-observed practice with caps, and feeds a deterministic Today planner (a `session` key added to GET /today) whose candidate/proposal contract the study-guide agent later fills. A progress dashboard, staged waiting states, a ready notifier, empty states, one honesty chip and a linear path and stage page complete the track. Every step is additive, keeps existing response keys, and names the specs it changes. Nothing here was run: the plan is based on reading the code and tests.

key_decisions.choice: New table `learner_profiles` (PK `learner_id`, FK learners ON DELETE CASCADE), created lazily by `profile.service.ensure()` with insert-on-conflict-do-nothing. Columns: stage_id, stage_source, daily_goal_points, support_mode, gloss_mode, stated_goal (enum, no free text), onboarded_at. Migration 0008 backfills one row per existing learner with the stage from `story_series.stage_id` and `onboarded_at` NULL, so the owner sees the new start once with the current level pre-selected.
key_decisions.why: `learners` is updated on every request (identity/service.py:28) and locked NOWAIT by topic_conversations/service.py:106. Migration 0001 gave it no server defaults, and tests construct `Learner(subject, email)` directly. A separate table is purely additive, is ignored by old code during the migration-first release, and gives the snapshot and agents one typed row. An enum goal avoids passing learner free text into agent prompts.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Columns on `learners` (each needs a Python default plus a server_default and widens the hottest row). A JSONB preferences blob (untyped, no constraints). Backfilling existing learners as already onboarded (less disruptive, but the owner who called the start confusing would never meet the fix; it is a one-line change in the migration if preferred).

key_decisions.choice: `learner_profiles.stage_id` is the only level. `profile.service.set_stage` is the only writer. `story_series.stage_id` stays as a cache updated in the same transaction. `stories.default_stage` reads the profile (default 'a1'). POST /stories/level stays as an alias. The PracticeCoach localStorage key and the path's first-unpassed rule are removed. Self-placement writes `stage_source='self_placement'` and touches no CurriculumAttempt or CurriculumPractice row. Moving up is learner-confirmed: GET /me returns `suggested_stage_id` once the current stage's check is passed.
key_decisions.why: Keeps `test_default_level_skips_the_absolute_beginner_bridge` and the 'a1' assertion in `test_today_queues_an_episode...` green. A self-report can then never pass or unlock anything, and story difficulty never changes silently.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Deriving the level only from passed stages (this is the current pre-A1 path versus A1 stories conflict). Auto-promotion on a pass (a hidden change of story level). A placement test (it would imply a mastery claim on unreviewed content).

key_decisions.decision: Reconciling Learner.support_language with the web support modes
key_decisions.choice: `learner_profiles.support_mode` stores the web value ('nl-en' | 'nl-fa' | 'nl-fa-en', NULL = never synced). `LanguageProvider` keeps its localStorage `useSyncExternalStore` snapshot (keys `taalstudio.language-support` and new `taalstudio.profile-cache`). On load, a NULL server value means the local mode is uploaded once; otherwise the server wins and the cache is rewritten. `setMode` writes local and PATCHes /me. `learners.support_language` is kept as a mirror of the primary language ('en' for nl-en, else 'fa').
key_decisions.why: The owner's real preference lives only in the browser today, while the server default 'fa' was never chosen. A local cache keeps the first paint hydration-safe and working offline. GET /progress and GET /export keep their shape and become truthful.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Overloading `support_language` with mode strings (changes the meaning of an exported field). Server-only state (hydration flip on every load). Local-wins on conflict (devices overwrite each other on every visit).

key_decisions.choice: Client gate `components/shell/FirstRunGate.tsx` inside the shell. When GET /me succeeds with `onboarded_at` null and the path is not /welkom, /settings or /over, it renders a skeleton and calls `router.replace('/welkom')`. It fails open on any error. Today defers its own fetch until the profile settles, so GET /today is not called before the learner picks a level. `/welkom` renders in a bare variant of the shell (brand, language switcher, `main#main`), not a route-group move.
key_decisions.why: Every page already paints a client loading state, so a client gate adds no extra visible step. Playwright route fixtures can drive it. A server-side redirect would be the app's first server-to-API data path and would add a blocking hop per navigation on a 0.25 vCPU API. D-04 forbids cookies.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: `redirect()` in page.tsx or layout.tsx through a new server-side API helper. A cookie flag read in proxy.ts. A first-run branch inside TodayHome (deep links would skip it and the nav would still show).

key_decisions.decision: Pre-queuing the first episode without changing GET /today
key_decisions.choice: POST /me/onboarding stores the choices, syncs the series level and calls `stories.service.ensure_buffer`, so episode 1 is queued at the chosen level as soon as level and goal are known. The explainer and first activity (2-4 minutes) run while it is written. GET /today keeps calling `ensure_buffer` (a no-op once something is unread). One safety fix: `ensure_buffer` returns None while the newest episode is an unread failure, so page views stop creating paid retries.
key_decisions.why: About ten API tests and one unmocked e2e use GET /today to create the episode. The onboarding path adds a deliberate POST instead of moving the side effect. `test_a_persistently_bad_draft...` already accepts `episode is None` after a failure.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Moving the enqueue to a POST only (breaks test_stories.py:164-308 and stories.spec.ts:168-176). Gating the GET enqueue on `onboarded_at` (every test learner is new, so the same tests break). Queuing at account creation (wrong level before self-placement).

key_decisions.decision: Gloss layer: where it shows and when it fades
key_decisions.choice: `lib/ui-copy.ts` is a typed catalogue where every key needs nl, en and fa. `UiText` renders the Dutch line plus gloss lines by tier. Chrome (nav, buttons, tabs, chips) shows one gloss line (Persian if selected, else English). Guide (headings, instructions, benefit lines, empty states, errors) shows every selected language. Always (onboarding, explainer, honesty and points explanations) is always bilingual. `gloss_mode` auto means: all tiers for pre-A1 to A2, guide only for pre-B1 and B1, none from pre-B2. on/off override it. Glosses stay in the accessible name. `<html lang='nl'>` is unchanged.
key_decisions.why: Meets the owner's choice (Dutch chrome, gloss underneath, fading) without an i18n framework. One gloss line in chrome bounds tab height at 320 px. A typed catalogue is the single place to enforce 'je' and completeness with a unit test.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: A UI-locale switch (the owner rejected it). Tooltips (unusable on touch). Hiding glosses from the accessible name with aria-labelledby (the visible label would not match the name).

key_decisions.decision: Keeping about 70 class selectors, 164 testids and exact Dutch names stable
key_decisions.choice: Add auto-fixture `apps/web/tests/e2e/fixtures/test.ts`. Before each test it calls POST /api/me/onboarding (idempotent), then PATCH /api/me with support_mode 'nl-en', stage_id 'a1', daily_goal_points 20 and gloss_mode 'off'. All 18 specs import `test` and `expect` from it. New specs (gloss, onboarding, today, progress, navigation) turn glosses on or mock /api/me.
key_decisions.why: Profile state is now server-side and would leak between specs: curriculum.spec.ts sets 'nl-fa-en' through the switcher. With glosses off the existing chrome renders exactly as before, so only the selectors named per step change.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Seeding the profile once in scripts/run.py (state still leaks between specs). Test-only code paths in the app. Rewriting every name selector to tolerate glosses.

key_decisions.choice: `components/shell/nav.ts`: primaryNav = [{href:'/',key:'nav.today',icon:'home',mobile:true,match:[]},{href:'/leerpad',key:'nav.learn',icon:'path',mobile:true,match:['/learn/']},{href:'/verhalen',key:'nav.stories',icon:'book',mobile:true,match:['/verhalen/','/videos']},{href:'/spreken',key:'nav.speak',icon:'chat',mobile:true,match:['/missions','/speech-check']},{href:'/woorden',key:'nav.words',icon:'cards',mobile:true,match:[]},{href:'/progress',key:'nav.progress',icon:'chart',mobile:false,match:['/settings']}]. Labels nl/en/fa: Vandaag/Today/امروز, Leren/Learn/یادگیری, Verhalen/Stories and videos/داستان و ویدیو, Spreken/Speak/گفت‌وگو, Woorden/Words/واژه‌ها, Voortgang/Progress/پیشرفت. The header carries the language switcher, a progress chip linking to /progress and a profile link to /settings at every width. Routes /videos, /missions, /speech-check and /settings keep their URLs and become second-level pages (MediaTabs, the /spreken hub, AccountTabs).
key_decisions.why: Five mobile tabs instead of six at 9 px, one home for speaking (where the conversation partner and live voice land later), and no URL changes, so deep links and most specs survive. Every destination remains an `<a href>` inside `div.app-frame`, which is all the guard intercepts.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: A drawer or 'More' menu (portal or button navigation bypasses the click-capture guard, and hidden links fail resilience.spec). Folding Woorden into Leren (daily review loses its tab). Merging /videos into /verhalen as one route (breaks videos.spec for no gain).

key_decisions.choice: Existing values are unchanged: episode_read 10, episode_answer 3 per correct, episode_choice 2, read_aloud 5, word_review 1, video_watch 10, video_answer 3 per correct. New kinds: lesson_practice 6 (reading/listening) or 8 (speaking/writing); topic_practice 6 or 8; conversation 2 per learner reply, at most 12; mission_turn 2; mission_step 4; stage_check 15; speech_warmup 2; reserved for P4: exercise_item 1 and exercise_session 5. Zero points: saving words, hints and help, writing-feedback requests, self-assessed recall rounds. `record_activity(session, learner_id, kind, points=None, ref='', request_id='', *, skill=None, stage_id='', units=1, meta=None, day=None)` takes the value from `activity/rules.py` when `points` is None and clamps caller values to the rule maximum.
key_decisions.why: Keeping old values keeps the pinned totals (16, 18, 13, 10, 5, 1) green. New kinds pay for completion only, at roughly two points per minute, so a 20-point goal is about ten minutes of any mix. A central table means code decides and the dashboard can explain the rules from the same data.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Callers choosing their own values (the current scattered POINTS dicts). Paying for model-judged quality (passed, criteria met, accepted) — that would judge the learner's Dutch. Re-pricing existing kinds now (breaks about ten tests for no learner benefit).

key_decisions.choice: Idempotency is a unique (learner_id, kind, dedupe_key), with scope per rule. Once per ref: episode, video, paragraph, conversation, turn, session step, attempt. Once per ref per Brussels day: lesson_practice per stage+skill, topic_practice per topic+skill, speech_warmup. word_review is each request, limited to 2 awards per word per day. Daily caps: word_review 30, topic_practice 24, mission_turn 20, exercise_item 30. Capped or duplicate events are still stored with 0 points. Only server-observed events earn points. The daily goal is the learner's choice (10, 20 or 30; default 20), frozen per day in `learning_days.goal_target`. The streak tolerates one rest day in any seven days and nothing can be bought back.
key_decisions.why: The current uncapped word review (an 'again' card returns after 10 minutes) is farmable. Caps protect the meaning of the goal without punishing. A frozen target keeps history stable when the goal changes. A rest day makes the streak non-punitive, and the pinned streak test (offsets 1, 2, 3, 6, 7) still yields 3 and then 4.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Hearts, lives or streak freezes bought with points (the owner excluded these). Diminishing-returns formulas (hard to explain in plain language). Time-on-page points (client-claimed, unverifiable).

key_decisions.decision: Today plan contract the study-guide agent must satisfy
key_decisions.choice: `session = {version:'today-plan-v1', source:'planner'|'study_guide', date, stage_id, target_points, earned_points, estimated_minutes, steps:[{id, candidate_id, kind, skill, status:'todo'|'active'|'done'|'waiting'|'blocked', title, benefit, reason, basis, minutes, points, href, action, meta}], primary:{step_id, href, label}|null, summary}`; all texts are {nl,en,fa}. Code builds the candidate pool (ids, kinds, hrefs, minutes, points, status and the set of true `basis` facts per candidate). A proposal may only be `{order:[candidate_id], reasons:{candidate_id:{basis,nl,en,fa}}, summary}`. `validate_proposal` enforces: ids from the pool, no duplicates, 2-5 steps, minutes within the goal budget (10→8, 20→15, 30→25), at least two skills, warm-up first when words are due, a basis that is true in the snapshot, reasons of at most 160 characters with no digits beyond the candidate's meta. A failed check returns the planner's plan.
key_decisions.why: The agent can change order and wording but never hrefs, points, minutes, status or completion, so the UI and tests do not change when P6 swaps the source. Reasons are grounded in enumerated snapshot facts rather than free claims.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Letting the agent emit steps or links freely (invented activities). A separate endpoint for the agent plan (two shapes to render). Keeping `next_step` as the contract (single enum, no reasons, stories and words only).

key_decisions.decision: Waiting states and the ready notification
key_decisions.choice: `WaitingCard` shows real stages from fields already in `episode_view(full=False)`: queued → 'in de wachtrij', generating with attempts ≤1 → 'de schrijver schrijft', generating with attempts 2 → 'herschrijven na controle', then ready. The planner puts non-waiting steps first, so the learner starts the warm-up meanwhile. `ReadyNotifier` polls the side-effect-free GET /today/ready every 15 s only while something is pending and the tab is visible, then shows an in-frame toast link and a dot on the Verhalen tab.
key_decisions.why: The stages are honest (derived from stored status). The poll is three cheap SELECTs instead of GET /today every 5 s with its row locks and enqueue path. The toast is an anchor inside `.app-frame`, so the guard applies.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: SSE or WebSocket push (the proxy drops Last-Event-ID, and one sync replica is involved; the SSE helper is reserved for streamed replies). Browser notifications (permission prompts). A fake percentage bar.

key_decisions.decision: How far the path and stage pages are restructured
key_decisions.choice: Structure only. Path: `CurrentStageHero` plus a compact always-visible `StageRail` that keeps `data-testid=curriculum-path`, twelve `li` and the `Open {label}: {title}` link names. Stage: `LessonStepper` with a persistent 'Volgende stap'; the core lesson is the default; the toggle is renamed 'Les | Meer oefenen'; the nav name 'Onderdelen van dit niveau' and its button names are unchanged; `?stap=` selects a step. Lesson content and grading are left to the P4 exercise engine.
key_decisions.why: Delivers the linear feel now, while the spec impact is a mechanical rename ('Startles' → 'Les' in 10 places, one helper edit, five 'Story Time' strings) and P4 can replace section bodies without touching the stepper.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Collapsing other stages into a closed `<details>` (the links become hidden and three specs fail `toBeVisible`). Rewriting lesson sections now (collides with P4). A separate route per step (breaks every /learn deep link in the specs).

Hand-written op.create_table in the style of 0006/0007, with a server_default on every NOT NULL column. Backfill: INSERT ... SELECT l.id, COALESCE(s.stage_id,'a1'), CASE WHEN s.id IS NULL THEN 'default' ELSE 'legacy_series' END ... FROM learners l LEFT JOIN story_series s ON s.learner_id = l.id, with onboarded_at and support_mode NULL. Downgrade drops the table. Additive: old code ignores it. data_model.name: activity_events (new)
data_model.fields: id UUID PK; learner_id UUID FK learners.id ON DELETE CASCADE; day Date NOT NULL (Europe/Brussels day of the event); kind String(40) NOT NULL; skill String(12) NOT NULL default '' (reading | listening | speaking | writing | vocabulary | ''); stage_id String(20) NOT NULL default ''; ref String(120) NOT NULL default ''; request_id String(80) NOT NULL default ''; dedupe_key String(200) NOT NULL (built by code from ref, day or request_id according to the rule's scope); points Integer NOT NULL default 0 (0 when capped); units Integer NOT NULL default 1; meta JSONB NOT NULL default {} (ids and counts only, never learner text); created_at timestamptz NOT NULL. Repeat calls change nothing and queue nothing. It never touches CurriculumAttempt or CurriculumPractice. If an unread failed episode exists, `episode` is null and the web shows the retry state.

constraints_revised.rule: D-19: only reading, answering, choosing, reading aloud and reviewing words earn points; the daily goal is twenty points; a missed day resets the streak.
constraints_revised.revision: New entry 'Points for all practice (revises D-19)': Every kind of practice the server can observe earns points for the Europe/Brussels day: episodes and videos, choosing, reading aloud, word review, a core-lesson or topic activity in any of the four skills, replies in a guided conversation or mission, a finished exercise session and a completed stage check. Each award is one append-only row in activity_events (unique per learner, kind and reference); the day row in learning_days is updated in the same transaction. Points still reward doing and never judge the learner's Dutch: values are fixed per kind in activity/rules.py, a model's verdict never changes them, and wrong answers cost nothing. Once-per-item rules and per-kind daily caps limit repetition; capped events are stored with zero points. The daily goal is the learner's choice (10, 20 or 30; default 20) and is frozen per day. The streak counts consecutive active days and tolerates one rest day in any seven; nothing is bought back. There are no hearts, lives, levels or leagues.

design.track: Visual design system and interactivity (P1 foundation, applied through P2-P4, closed out in P8)
design.approach_summary:
Root: C:\Users\Nima\Desktop\MINE\My_projects\Dutch Learning Platform\Final_Project_v1 (paths below are relative to it).

The redesign is sequenced so every structural change is provably invisible before any visible change lands. First freeze the current UI with Linux-only Playwright baselines and a ratcheting CSS guard test. Then delete dead CSS by selector, wrap the ten stylesheets in one `legacy` cascade layer, and introduce a single `apps/web/app/styles/tokens.css` whose compat aliases reproduce today's effective values (all zero-diff). Only then flip palette, type scale and focus ring through tokens, which re-skins every legacy screen with almost no TSX churn and keeps the ~70 e2e class selectors intact.

Styling decision: token-driven global classes in cascade layers (`reset, tokens, base, components, legacy, features, utilities`) with typed React wrappers in `components/ui`; CSS Modules only for screen-private layout of new features; Tailwind rejected. Colour is semantic: brand blue for actions, one hue per skill/section applied with `data-accent`, green/red reserved for feedback, every pair checked at AA by a unit test. Motion is CSS-only with reduced-motion fallbacks; overlays use native dialog/popover; icons move to lucide-react behind the existing `Icon` facade; illustrations are inline SVG, so the CSP stays 'self'.

Primitives, shell, Today, path map, exercise feedback and word cards are then applied phase by phase, each step ending with axe, overflow, unit and visual gates green. Dark mode is prepared at token level only. Nothing was run or built in this worktree (node_modules is absent); contrast ratios were computed, bundler behaviour was read from the Next 16.3 docs.

key_decisions.choice: Token-driven global classes in cascade layers. Each shared primitive has one global CSS file under apps/web/app/styles/ui/ in @layer components, wrapped by a typed component in apps/web/components/ui; state is expressed with data-state / data-tone / data-accent attributes. CSS Modules are allowed only for screen-private layout of NEW feature components (file starts with the layer statement, rules inside @layer features, no keyframes inside). No Tailwind.
key_decisions.why: Class names are a public contract in this repo: .button has about 106 TSX call sites (many on Link/span and in server pages), .card 39, .error 39, .eyebrow 49, and about 70 class selectors are used by e2e. Canonical global classes let P1 re-skin every screen CSS-only and keep specs green by construction. Layers remove the import-order dependence that produced three stacked redesigns. CSP does not discriminate between the options (static CSS from 'self'; inline style custom properties are already allowed by style-src 'unsafe-inline' in apps/web/proxy.ts).
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: CSS Modules for primitives: hashed names break the legacy/e2e contract, and Next 16 Turbopack (Lightning CSS) documents no support for composes from a global .css file or standalone :global, so bridging to legacy classes is awkward. Tailwind v4: new PostCSS toolchain, its own theme/base/components/utilities layers and preflight would fight the legacy layer, a rewrite of about 1,190 rule blocks, and longer className strings in JSX that already has 1,000-character lines. Unlayered global CSS as today: keeps the cascade accident.

key_decisions.decision: Cascade layer order and how the ten existing files are wrapped
key_decisions.choice: apps/web/app/styles/layers.css holds exactly `@layer reset, tokens, base, components, legacy, features, utilities;` and is the first CSS import in apps/web/app/layout.tsx. globals.css, design.css, learning.css, learning-tools.css, library.css, phrase-audio.css, topics.css, learning-agents.css, stories.css, videos.css are each wrapped in the SAME `@layer legacy { ... }`, import order unchanged. components sits BEFORE legacy. The reduced-motion and print blocks (design.css:1684-1711) move to reset.
key_decisions.why: One shared legacy layer preserves today's specificity-then-order result exactly; per-file sublayers would not (globals.css:163 .button:focus-visible currently beats design.css:59 :focus-visible by specificity). components before legacy keeps the many contextual overrides working (.continue-copy .button, .practice-source-switch .button, .read-aloud.is-recording .button, .unit-test-card .button, .catalog-card .button), provided the bare duplicate definitions are deleted when the canonical one lands. For !important declarations the earliest layer wins, so the reduced-motion neutraliser in reset beats everything. Wrapping each file explicitly avoids depending on @import ... layer().
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: legacy before components (canonical primitives would flatten every contextual legacy override regardless of specificity); one sublayer per file (changes behaviour); leaving legacy unlayered (unlayered rules beat all layers, so new code could never win without specificity hacks).

key_decisions.decision: Token file structure (apps/web/app/styles/tokens.css, the only file allowed to contain colour literals)
key_decisions.choice: Three tiers. (1) Primitive ramps --slate-*, --blue-*, --teal-*, --violet-*, --orange-*, --amber-*, --rose-*, --green-*, --red-*; never used by components. (2) Semantic tokens on :root: surfaces --surface-canvas #f6f8fc, --surface-raised #fff, --surface-sunken #eef2f8, --surface-inverse #1c3558, --surface-disabled #e3e9f2; text --text #14243b, --text-muted #4f5d73, --text-subtle #5d6c82, --text-disabled #76859b, --text-on-solid #fff, --text-muted-on-inverse #c2d1e8, --text-link #2455b5; borders --border #d3dbe7 (decorative), --border-strong #76859b (form controls); actions --action-solid #2455b5, --action-solid-hover #1b448f, --action-edge #163872; feedback --success|warning|danger|info-{bg,ink,border,solid,vivid} = 50/700/200/600/500 of green/amber/red/blue; --recording-{bg,ink,pulse} from red. (3) Local accent roles set by explicit [data-accent=...] blocks: --accent-solid (600), --accent-solid-hover (700), --accent-ink (700), --accent-ink-strong (800), --accent-subtle (50), --accent-muted (100), --accent-border (200), --accent-vivid (500). Plus temporary compat aliases --bg, --surface, --ink, --muted, --line, --accent, --accent-ink, --ok-*, --warn-*, --bad-*, --radius, --warm*, --tone-*.
key_decisions.why: Semantic names are what a dark theme and the contrast test operate on. Accent roles are written out per accent (not derived on :root) because a custom property that references var() is resolved where it is declared; deriving on :root would freeze every accent to brand blue. Primary actions use --action-* (always brand blue) so buttons stay consistent while identity, selection and progress take the section hue. Compat aliases let the three legacy :root blocks disappear without touching 2,800 lines.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: A TS/JSON token source with a build step (new tooling for no gain; the unit test parses the CSS directly); section-coloured primary buttons (multiplies contrast permutations and reads as inconsistent).

key_decisions.why: Anchored on what exists so the change reads as an evolution: blue-600 is today's --accent #2455b5, slate follows --ink #182c47/--muted/--line, orange/rose/violet/teal/amber follow the stories.css tone pairs. Steps are assigned by role so one rule works for every hue: 600 carries white text, 700 is text on white or on the 50 tint, 500 is for graphics.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Keeping the 356 literal hex values; using today's --warm #d9672b as a text-bearing fill (white on it is 3.54:1, fails AA); keeping #f2b233 as the focus colour (1.88:1 on white).

key_decisions.decision: Hue assignment and the contrast pairs it must pass (computed with the WCAG formula)
key_decisions.choice: reading/Lezen, path, today = blue; listening/Luisteren, videos = teal; speaking/Spreken, conversations, speech studio = violet; writing/Schrijven = orange; words/Woorden, alphabet = amber; stories/Verhalen = rose; progress = green; grammar, settings = slate. Pairs (white on 600 | 700 on its 50 tint | 700 on 100 | 500 graphic on white / on 50): blue 6.90 | 8.38 | 7.50 | 4.71 / 4.26; teal 5.36 | 6.73 | 5.95 | 3.83 / 3.45; violet 6.70 | 8.07 | 6.94 | 5.33 / 4.71; orange 4.72 | 6.28 | 5.59 | 3.68 / 3.38; amber 5.17 | 6.07 | 5.49 | 3.46 / 3.26; rose 5.67 | 6.84 | 5.99 | 4.15 / 3.70; green 5.37 | 6.80 | 5.98 | 3.48 / 3.15; red 5.85 | 7.03 | 6.02 | 4.30 / 3.81. Neutrals: --text on canvas 14.68; --text-muted on canvas 6.28, on sunken 5.94; --text-subtle on canvas 5.02, on sunken 4.75 (not allowed on slate-100); --border-strong on white 3.75, on sunken 3.34; white on --surface-inverse 12.36; --text-muted-on-inverse 7.99. Rule: 600 is for fills and large text only (orange-600 on orange-50 is 4.33); text on tints uses 700/800.
key_decisions.why: Four skills get four well-separated hues that are neither success-green nor danger-red, so identity never collides with correctness. Sections reuse the related skill hue (videos with listening, conversations with speaking) to keep the palette to eight families. Skill identity is always icon + label + colour, never colour alone (blue/violet and teal/green are weak for some colour-vision types).
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Review suggestion of green for listening (collides with success); a ninth indigo for grammar (too close to blue and violet); amber-500 #d99a00 as a graphic colour (2.45:1 on white).

key_decisions.decision: Scales: type, spacing, radius, elevation, motion, z-index, breakpoints
key_decisions.choice: Type (html stays 16px; body moves 15px -> 1rem): --text-xs 0.75rem (floor; eyebrows, badges, tab labels), --text-sm 0.875rem, --text-md 1rem, --text-lg 1.125rem (Dutch practice text), --text-xl 1.25rem, --text-2xl 1.5rem, --text-3xl clamp(1.75rem, 1.35rem + 1.7vw, 2.375rem), --text-display clamp(2.25rem, 1.5rem + 3.2vw, 3.5rem); leading 1.2/1.4/1.6/1.9 (1.9 for reading and Persian); weights 400/550/650; --tracking-caps .06em. Space --space-1..16 = .25/.5/.75/1/1.25/1.5/2/2.5/3/4rem; --target-min 2.75rem; --measure 68ch. Radius --radius-xs 6px, -sm 10px, -md 14px, -lg 20px, -xl 28px, -pill 999px. Elevation --shadow-1 0 1px 2px rgb(20 36 59/.06), --shadow-2 0 4px 14px rgb(20 36 59/.08), --shadow-3 0 14px 36px rgb(20 36 59/.14), --edge 0 2px 0 var(--action-edge). Motion --dur-1 80ms, -2 140ms, -3 220ms, -4 420ms, -5 900ms; --ease-out cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1), --ease-in-out cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1), --ease-spring cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1). z-index --z-raised 1, --z-sticky 100, --z-sidebar 200, --z-nav 300, --z-overlay 500, --z-toast 600, --z-skip 700. Breakpoints (constants enforced by test, since custom properties cannot be used in media queries): 480, 768, 1050, 1280; container queries for tiles.
key_decisions.why: About 30 live declarations are 7-10px today; radii range 2-22px; there are 14 breakpoints and five ad-hoc z-index values. The z-index scale also fixes a real defect: .skip-link:focus has z-index 10 (globals.css:46-50) under .app-sidebar z-index 20 (design.css:79) and the sticky header z-index 18 (learning.css:25), so the focused skip link is painted underneath them; the e2e test only checks focus, not visibility.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Keeping px sizes (ignores user font settings); an 11px exception for uppercase labels (the owner asked for a 12px floor); @custom-media (needs a non-default Lightning CSS flag).

key_decisions.decision: Correct/incorrect colours under the non-punitive rule
key_decisions.choice: Correct = success set (green-50 bg, green-700 ink, green-500 2px border, check icon). Incorrect = danger set at subtle strength only (red-50 bg, red-700 ink, red-500 border, x icon), never a solid red fill; the correct option then shows state reveal (dashed green-500 border + label 'Juiste antwoord'). Tokens --answer-correct-* and --answer-incorrect-* alias the feedback sets so the choice can change in one place. Shake is at most 4px, once. Copy stays constructive ('Nog niet. Bekijk de uitleg.'). No hearts, no score ring, no accent/pronunciation meter anywhere in the kit.
key_decisions.why: Selected state uses the skill accent, so feedback must use hues no skill owns; green and red are the only two. Today's amber 'try again' (.practice-hint, .is-wrong) would be indistinguishable from 'selected' inside an orange writing exercise or an amber word exercise. Icon + text + border style carry the state for colour-blind users.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Amber/orange for incorrect (collides with writing and words accents and with warning notices); solid red blocks (punitive).

key_decisions.choice: base.css: `:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus-ring); outline-offset: 2px; }` with --focus-ring #2455b5; inside [data-surface=inverse] --focus-ring is #ffffff; #main keeps outline none (skip target); forced-colors uses Highlight. All other outline declarations are removed (globals.css:163-169 and 286 #f2b233, design.css:59-62 #ad7b26, phrase-audio.css:5 #527baa, learning-agents.css:19 #245d9b) and forbidden by the guard test.
key_decisions.why: The ring learners actually see today on links, .button, input and textarea is #f2b233 at 1.88:1 on white. #2455b5 measures 6.90 on white, 6.49 on canvas and at least 5.25 on every 100-step tint; white on the navy hero is 12.36. The 2px offset keeps it distinct from 2px accent selection borders. axe does not test focus indicators, so the token test covers it.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Dark ink ring (invisible on the navy panels without a second rule and heavier than needed); two-tone box-shadow ring (collides with component shadows).

key_decisions.decision: Primitive inventory and states (components/ui, CSS in app/styles/ui)
key_decisions.choice: Button (primary/secondary/ghost/danger; md 44px, sm 36px visual with 44px hit area on coarse pointers; hover, active press, focus, disabled, aria-busy, aria-pressed; buttonClass() for Link). Card/Panel (raised/outlined/sunken/inverse/accent; data-interactive adds lift + press). Badge (neutral/accent/success/warning/danger/info/provisional) and Chip (toggle, aria-pressed). Notice (info/success/warning/danger/neutral; icon, title, body, actions; role status or alert). AnswerOption (default/hover/focus/selected/correct/incorrect/reveal/disabled over a native radio or checkbox). ProgressRing, ProgressBar (determinate/indeterminate/segmented), SkillMeter (four separate segments). Skeleton (line/block/circle, shimmer). EmptyState. IconTile (sm 36/md 44/lg 56, accent-tinted). Tabs (tablist, roving tabindex) and Segmented. Dialog/Sheet (native dialog). Toast (role=status provider). Stepper (ol/li/button[aria-current=step]). Extra: Field (input/textarea/select), Cover, Celebration, Gloss styles.
key_decisions.why: Each one replaces several divergent implementations that exist now: three .button definitions, five multiple-choice renderers, three correctness patterns, .practice-hint used for hints, successes and neutral notices, eight .path-loading text boxes, four empty-state styles, .practice-feedback.complete/.retry with no CSS. Existing class names stay on the same elements as the canonical names or as hooks.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Radix/shadcn (new dependency family; native dialog and popover cover the need and keep DOM inside .app-frame for the navigation guard); a separate Storybook (the dev-only /dev/ui gallery is enough and is testable with the existing e2e stack).

key_decisions.choice: Adopt lucide-react behind apps/web/components/Icon.tsx. Keep the props (name, size, className, style), aria-hidden default and server-component status; IconName becomes keyof a single `icons` map (existing 20 names remapped, about 25 added: flame, star, trophy, lock, message, sparkles, lightbulb, bookmark, refresh, check-circle, x-circle, alert, info, map, layers, target, eye, eye-off, shuffle, keyboard, pause, stop, plus, menu, more). strokeWidth 1.75. Pin an exact version after `npm view lucide-react version` (peer range covers React 19).
key_decisions.why: Icons currently cannot carry meaning: 'book' stands for Verhalen, Woorden, Lezen, Story Time and Praktijkgesprekken, 'check' is the Woorden tab. Four tracks will need roughly 60 glyphs; hand-drawing them in one file is slow and inconsistent. The facade means call sites never import the package, the bundle only contains mapped icons, and the dependency can be swapped in one file. Inline SVG, so CSP is untouched.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Extending the hand-written paths map (quality and effort); an icon font or sprite from a CDN (CSP is 'self' only); vendoring copied path data (viable zero-dependency fallback if the owner refuses the dependency: same facade, same names).

key_decisions.choice: Inline SVG React components in apps/web/components/illustrations/ (server components, aria-hidden, fills from currentColor and var(--accent-*)): StreetScene (De Lindestraat row houses), BookStack, SpeechBubbles, PathFlag, WordCards, Headphones, EmptyTray, Trophy. Plus a CSS-only Cover primitive generalising .episode-cover and coverClass() (TodayHome.tsx:13) with gradients var(--X-500) to var(--X-700) and three pattern variants. No apps/web/public directory. Any future raster asset is statically imported so it is served from /_next/static/media.
key_decisions.why: There is no public/ today; apps/web/Dockerfile copies only .next/standalone and .next/static, and the proxy.ts matcher would stamp public files with Cache-Control: private, no-store. Inline SVG is themeable (accent and later dark mode), needs no Dockerfile or proxy change and passes img-src 'self'. Gradients 500 to 700 keep large white cover text at 3.46:1 or better.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: public/illustrations/*.svg (needs Dockerfile and proxy matcher changes, not themeable); stock or generated raster art (weight, licence, no theming); Lottie (script and size).

key_decisions.choice: CSS only, in apps/web/app/styles/motion.css as keyframes plus [data-anim=...] utilities: press (:active translateY(2px) and edge shadow collapses, --dur-1), lift (hover translateY(-2px) + --shadow-2 on interactive cards), pop (scale 1 to 1.06 to 1, --ease-spring, correct option and ring completion), shake (4px, one cycle), fill (stroke-dashoffset / width transition --dur-4), flip (rotateY 180deg, backface hidden), pulse (expanding ring on .record-symbol, .mic-orbit.recording, .button.talk[aria-pressed=true]), shimmer (skeleton gradient), rise (toast), burst (14 spans with inline --dx/--dy/--r for goal and stage celebration). lib/client/motion.ts adds usePrefersReducedMotion and withViewTransition (document.startViewTransition when available, for tile moves). Reduced motion: the global neutraliser stays, plus explicit fallbacks: no burst nodes rendered (static badge instead), flip becomes a swap, pulse becomes a static ring.
key_decisions.why: Today there is one @keyframes, no :active rule and completion is plain text. Everything requested fits in CSS; inline custom properties on elements are permitted by the CSP. Celebrations fire only from server-reported events, which keeps the rule that code, not the client or a model, decides points and passes.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: motion/Framer Motion (about 30-50 kB and a second animation model for effects CSS already covers); canvas-confetti (extra dependency, canvas ignores reduced motion unless wrapped); animating via JS timers.

key_decisions.choice: Shell: sidebar items with accent-tinted IconTile, active = accent-subtle pill + accent-ink text + 3px inline-start bar; bottom tabs with an accent pill behind the active icon; 12px labels. Today: one hero next-step card tinted by the step accent with a single primary action and plain-language reasons, goal ProgressRing with flame and streak number (role=img name 'N dagen op rij' kept), seven-day strip, four small weekly-effort rings (one per skill, labelled as practice done, not level), first-run strip instead of zeros. Path: the same ol[data-testid=curriculum-path] with 12 li drawn as nodes on a connector (pseudo-elements, zig-zag from 768px, vertical timeline below), states passed/current/available only. Exercise feedback: AnswerOption states + FeedbackBar. Word cards: flip card with term, audio, meaning in the support languages, example with the term in <mark>, four tinted grade buttons.
key_decisions.why: These are the five places the owner's complaints land: unclear start, boring practice, no sense of progress. All use data the API already returns (streak, goal, recent_days, stage.passed, practice_completed) plus what the P3/P4 tracks add.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: A locked-node path (all levels are open and curriculum.spec.ts:10 asserts .stage-locked count 0); one overall progress ring or level badge (owner ruled out an overall level/CEFR claim); extra li elements for connectors (breaks the 12-li assertions).

key_decisions.choice: Tab bar uses grid-auto-flow: column with equal auto columns (replacing repeat(6, minmax(0,1fr)) at design.css:1333), 56px targets, no gloss line. While six tabs remain (P1), inactive labels become visually hidden below a 400px container width and the active tab shows its label; when the P2 navigation regroup lands on at most five tabs (four plus 'Meer' opening a Sheet rendered inside .app-frame), labels are always visible at 320px.

Links stay visible with their accessible names, so videos.spec.ts:155 (link Video's visible in 'Mobiel hoofdmenu' at 390px) still passes. A Sheet outside .app-frame would bypass the navigation guard (AppShell.tsx:71-108).

key_decisions.choice: (1) apps/web/tests/unit/design-tokens.test.mjs parses tokens.css, resolves var() chains and asserts every text pair at 4.5:1 and every graphic/border/focus pair at 3:1, for :root and for each [data-accent] block (and any future [data-theme] block). (2) apps/web/tests/unit/css-guard.test.mjs: in app/styles/** no colour literals outside tokens.css, no font-size under 0.75rem, no outline outside base.css, no z-index numerals, no !important outside reset.css, only the four breakpoints; per-file ratchet budgets for legacy files in css-budget.json that may only go down. (3) apps/web/tests/unit/css-usage.test.mjs: every class selector is referenced from TSX/TS (allowlist for tone-N, grade-*, status-*, kind-*, cover-N, is-*). (4) apps/web/tests/e2e/aa-visual.spec.ts with toHaveScreenshot at 1440/390/320, and ui-gallery.spec.ts for /dev/ui. (5) Existing axe and overflow gates unchanged and extended to the gallery.
key_decisions.why: axe checks rendered text contrast only on the screens specs visit, and never checks focus rings, borders or graphics; the token test covers the whole matrix cheaply. The ratchet turns '356 hex colours' into a number that can only fall. Zero-diff baselines prove the dead-CSS and layering steps are invisible.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: stylelint with plugins (new toolchain; the same rules fit in a dependency-free node:test file matching the existing tests/unit pattern); Chromatic/Percy (external service, paid, sends screenshots off the machine).

key_decisions.decision: How visual baselines stay deterministic and cross-platform
key_decisions.choice: Baselines are Linux-only: snapshotPathTemplate '{testDir}/__screenshots__/{arg}{ext}', the spec skips when process.platform is not linux unless VISUAL_LOCAL=1. The file is named aa-visual.spec.ts so it runs first on the learner that scripts/run.py task_e2e has just reset (mirrors the zz-reliability naming). page.clock.setFixedTime, /api/today and episode/word endpoints mocked from fixtures extracted out of stories.spec.ts, reducedMotion 'reduce', animations 'disabled', caret hidden, fonts awaited, maxDiffPixelRatio 0.002. scripts/run.py gains E2E_ARGS passthrough; ci.yml gains a workflow_dispatch input that runs with --update-snapshots and uploads __screenshots__ as an artifact for the owner to commit.
key_decisions.why: Playwright names snapshots per platform because rendering differs; the owner develops on Windows and CI is ubuntu. Workers are 1 and specs share one database, so a visual spec placed late would depend on side effects of earlier specs. The greeting changes with the hour and the unmocked Today always shows the animated 'writer is busy' card (JOB_LOOP_ENABLED=false).
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Per-platform baselines (doubles binaries and still differs between Windows machines); giving CI contents: write to commit baselines (widens CI permissions); screenshots as attachments only (what design.spec.ts does now; nothing fails on regressions).

key_decisions.choice: Components and features may reference semantic tokens only (enforced by css-guard). :root declares color-scheme: light. Shadows use one rgb channel token. The token test iterates theme blocks, so a later :root[data-theme=dark] block is validated the moment it is written. A dark value set is proposed in docs only until the legacy hex budget is zero: canvas #0f1a2b, raised #16243a, sunken #1d2f4a, text #e8eef7 (13.36 on raised), muted #a9b7cb (7.66), border-strong #5d7191 (3.14), accent ink from the 300/200 steps (blue-300 7.27). No prefers-color-scheme rule and no toggle in this plan.
key_decisions.why: A token-only retheme would leave most of the UI light while 356 literals remain, and axe/visual gates only cover light. Shipping the structure now makes dark a values-only change later.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Shipping a dark theme in P1 (untestable until legacy CSS is tokenised); light-dark() everywhere now (fine later; today it would double the contrast matrix before the light system is stable).

design.track: Code and structure modernisation for API and web (P0 tooling and quick fixes, P5 prerequisites, P8 hardening)
design.approach_summary:
All paths are relative to C:\Users\Nima\Desktop\MINE\My_projects\Dutch Learning Platform\Final_Project_v1. Sixteen steps, each built expand-then-contract so CI stays green.

Pull early (prerequisites for other tracks): S01 formatter before the P1 re-skin; S02 contract and boundary ratchets and S04 error codes before any new endpoint (P2 /me, P3 activity, P4 exercises); S05 skills/stages registry for P1 colours and P2 level; S06 query layer for P2/P3 screens; S08 pure GET /today before the P3 Today rebuild; S09 LlmGateway, S11 lease heartbeat, S12 SSE seam and S13 model-call telemetry before any P6 agent. Later hardening: S10 (tail of call-site migration), S14 layering, S15 component splits, S16 delivery.

The API stays synchronous: SSE uses sync generators (the routes_videos.py precedent); only Voice Live needs one async WebSocket router. Billing moves into the gateway's own short transaction with one failure policy. Domain errors become typed with stable codes and an explicit persist flag that replaces the return-not-raise convention. Provider failures become 503; 502 is reserved for the proxy. The web keeps apiFetch (ConnectionBanner contract) under TanStack Query, generated OpenAPI types and Vitest. Server prefetch starts with /me only, because e2e mocks run in the browser.

Two things I checked changed the plan: FastAPI's current docs say yield-dependencies exit after the response is sent by default (so today's commit is invisible to the client), and aborting the proxy fetch cannot stop a sync route already running in the threadpool. Nothing here was executed; every step needs its tests run.

key_decisions.choice: Keep every route sync def. SSE endpoints are sync routes returning StreamingResponse over a sync generator (precedent: api/routes_videos.py:106-121). The only async code is one WebSocket router for Voice Live (P7), which calls the same sync use-cases through anyio.to_thread.
key_decisions.why: 13.4k lines of sync SQLAlchemy and domain code serve one learner; converting buys nothing visible. A sync generator gives token streaming with no new infrastructure, and each stream costs one threadpool worker out of 40.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Full async conversion (AsyncSession, async adapters): a rewrite of every domain and about 328 tests. A separate streaming microservice: a second deployable and a second trust boundary for a single-user app.

key_decisions.choice: LlmGateway reserves and settles through its own short session_scope (separate connection), never the request session. One policy table: ProviderUnavailable or new ProviderRejected (non-retryable 4xx) releases; any other failure charges the token estimate and the attempts made; success charges tokens summed over attempts and HTTP attempts as model_calls.
key_decisions.why: Today about 11 sites disagree (release in practice/turns.py:178, feedback, curriculum, writing; commit-estimate in stories, videos, coaching, content_review, topic conversations). usage_counters row locks are held across provider calls, so a second paid request waits 30 s and becomes a 500. Own-session settlement removes both and makes billing independent of return-versus-raise.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Keep reservations in the request transaction with a shared helper: keeps the lock problem and the hidden commit convention. An outbox or event table for billing: more machinery than a second short transaction.

key_decisions.choice: Body stays {detail, request_id} plus stable `code` and optional `params`; content type stays application/json. Every provider failure from the API is 503 (provider_unavailable, provider_failed, turn_failed). 502 is emitted only by the Next proxy (api_unreachable) with header x-proxy-error; 504 upstream_timeout is also proxy-only.
key_decisions.why: lib/client/api.ts:67 treats any 502 as 'API down', so a failed practice turn currently raises the ConnectionBanner. The web shows raw English detail strings in a Dutch UI; codes let errorMessage() return nl/en/fa copy for the gloss layer. Keeping `detail` means existing tests and components keep working during the additive commit.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: RFC 9457 problem+json media type: no consumer benefits and it risks content-type assertions. Keeping 502 for uncertain failures: status would stay ambiguous with the proxy. Per-router mappers: three already diverged.

key_decisions.choice: DomainError carries persist: bool. get_session commits when a persisting DomainError passes through, rolls back otherwise. Routes switch to SessionDep = Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session, scope='function')] so the success commit runs before the response is sent.
key_decisions.why: Three pinned behaviours depend on returning a JSONResponse instead of raising (routes_practice.py:158-165 and 308-311, routes_curriculum.py:61-63). FastAPI's documented default scope is 'request', which runs exit code after the response is sent, so a failed commit is invisible and a follow-up GET can race the write.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Explicit session.commit() before each raise: easy to forget and scattered. Keeping the convention: invisible at call sites and incompatible with one set of exception handlers.

key_decisions.choice: Request path: new claim -> call -> settle helper (dlp/llm/claims.py, table call_claims, insert-or-409) for all new paid endpoints and for sites as they are touched. Job handlers keep their FOR UPDATE at-most-once guard for now and gain a lease heartbeat, so a live worker can no longer be reclaimed.
key_decisions.why: test_content_review.py:266 pins the lock-held guard, and jobs run on one background thread holding one connection, so the cost is low. The heartbeat removes the real hazard (a 60 s lease against 120 s x 3 calls) without rewriting three handlers. Streaming agent endpoints must not hold locks, so they are born two-phase.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Rewriting stories, videos and content_review to compare-and-swap claims now: high risk, little benefit for one learner. Session-level advisory locks held across the call: still pins a pooled connection.

key_decisions.choice: Export openapi.json in CI from create_app().openapi() (not served in production), generate apps/web/lib/api/schema.d.ts with openapi-typescript 7, fail on diff. Response models use extra=forbid. A ratchet test lists legacy untyped routes and may only shrink; every new route must declare response_model. Keep apiJson as the client.
key_decisions.why: Other tracks add many endpoints; the contract must exist before them. Request bodies are already Pydantic, so generated types pay off immediately. extra=forbid turns drift into a failing test instead of silently dropped fields.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Converting all routes at once: views return ad-hoc dicts with optional keys and would 500 on drift. openapi-fetch or a generated client: would bypass apiFetch and the dlp:connectivity events that resilience.spec.ts pins. zod at the boundary: a second schema source.

key_decisions.choice: pyright in CI on an include-list of new modules (dlp/errors.py, dlp/llm, dlp/api/errors.py, dlp/api/sse.py, then activity, exercises and agents as they appear), basic mode first.
key_decisions.why: It infers Pydantic v2 and SQLAlchemy 2 Mapped[] types without plugins and is fast enough to run on every push. A ratchet avoids a large clean-up of legacy modules.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: mypy: needs the pydantic plugin and more configuration for the same coverage. Whole-codebase strict typing now: large diff with no learner value.

key_decisions.choice: TanStack Query v5 whose query functions call the existing typed client objects (stories, videos, words) so apiFetch, X-Request-Id reuse and connectivity events are untouched. Typed key factory in lib/client/query-keys.ts. No focus refetch, GET retry only on 503/504, mutations never auto-retry.
key_decisions.why: It removes fetch-in-effect, the JSON.stringify keyed-result guard, three hand-rolled pollers and four duplicate /curriculum fetches, and gives invalidation (saving a word refreshes Today). The 'no state-setting in effects' rule becomes easier to follow: server state is never copied into useState.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: SWR: weaker mutation and invalidation model for the exercise and agent flows. A home-made hook: re-implements cache, dedupe and polling. keepPreviousData on pagers: would violate the pinned 'no updated pager with stale cards' test in library-writing.spec.ts.

key_decisions.choice: lib/server/api.ts::serverApiJson for an allowlist of side-effect-free GETs, starting with `me` in the root layout (HydrationBoundary). Today joins only after S08 and after the P3 track rewrites stories.spec.ts to use real fixture data.
key_decisions.why: Playwright page.route mocks run in the browser; a server-side fetch bypasses them, so prefetching /today now would break the three mocked Today tests. /me is new, has no mocks, removes the Persian-mode flash and gives every page the profile without a round trip.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Converting pages to RSC data fetching wholesale: breaks most mocked specs. A test-only header to disable SSR: test-specific production code.

key_decisions.choice: Expand: add idempotent POST /today/prepare (ensure_buffer plus the same payload) and make TodayHome load through it. Contract: GET /today becomes read-only and tests switch through one helper.
key_decisions.why: A side-effect-free GET that still returns episode_count == 1 on first call is impossible, so the pinned tests must change; doing it in two commits keeps CI green and keeps the e2e 'real API queues the first episode' passing.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Leaving the side effect: blocks server prefetch and lets prefetches or extra tabs enqueue paid work. Enqueueing at learner creation: still a write on a GET.

key_decisions.choice: Prettier 3 with eslint-config-prettier, one isolated format commit recorded in .git-blame-ignore-revs, CI format:check.
key_decisions.why: ESLint with eslint-config-next stays the linter; Prettier is the conventional pairing and preserves JSX whitespace semantics, which matters for exact-text e2e locators.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Biome: would replace or duplicate the Next ESLint rules the project relies on. No formatter: 1,000-3,300 character JSX lines make every later diff unreviewable.

key_decisions.choice: Vitest + React Testing Library + jsdom for components and hooks, alongside the existing node:test .mjs suite, plus tsconfig.test.json so specs are type-checked.
key_decisions.why: node --experimental-strip-types cannot resolve '@/...' aliases, React, or parameter properties (ApiError), so api.ts and every component are untestable today. The six existing suites are fast and valuable, so they stay.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Migrating the node:test suites: churn without benefit. MSW: an extra dependency when vi.stubGlobal('fetch') with the e2e payloads is enough.

key_decisions.choice: Keep the PostgreSQL queue and in-process JobLoop; add JobContext injection, lease heartbeat, conditional completion, retention and metrics; add `run-jobs --loop` so the same image can run as a worker app behind a Bicep flag that defaults to off.
key_decisions.why: One replica and one learner do not justify a broker; the real defects are the unrenewed lease, import-side-effect registration and unbounded table. The worker flag is the escape hatch before API replicas scale or ffmpeg needs CPU.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Service Bus or Celery: new paid resource and contradicts LEARNING_AGENTS.md:97. A thread pool in the API process now: more concurrency against 0.25 vCPU and a 10-connection pool.

key_decisions.choice: CI (main) pushes dlp-api and dlp-web to GHCR and records digests; deploy.yml imports those digests into ACR with `az acr import` and deploys them. CI still has no Azure sign-in.
key_decisions.why: The deployed image is then the one CI built from that commit rather than a second build. The docs show az acr import accepts a source by digest and credentials for non-Azure private registries.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Azure OIDC login in CI to push straight to ACR: gives every push Azure credentials, against the current 'no Azure sign-in in CI' stance. Keeping az acr build in deploy: a rebuild.

key_decisions.choice: Move migration job, API, web and auth config to infra/apps.bicep, which needs no secret values (apps reference Key Vault secrets by URL). azure_release.py runs the migration, then applies the module with image digests as parameters.
key_decisions.why: New settings for agents, voice and sizing would otherwise be added through imperative --set-env-vars and drift from Bicep. Splitting the module avoids re-supplying the secure parameters of main.bicep on every release.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Re-deploying all of main.bicep per release: needs every secret each time. Staying imperative: configuration drift grows with each track.

open_risks: FastAPI dependency scope: the current docs describe Depends(scope='function'|'request') with 'request' (exit after the response is sent) as the default. I did not run it against the locked fastapi 0.141.1 / starlette 1.6.0, and its interaction with context_dep sharing get_session is unproven. S08 starts with a spike test; if it fails, fall back to an explicit commit in a small wrapper around route execution.

SSE buffering under `next start`: whether Next's compression buffers text/event-stream is unverified. S12 adds an e2e test and two fallbacks (Cache-Control: no-transform, then compress: false). The Container Apps ingress has a 240 s request timeout, so agent streams must be bounded well below it.

Aborting the proxy request does not cancel a sync FastAPI route already executing; paid work for an abandoned non-streaming request still completes and is charged. Only streaming endpoints stop early. This is accepted and documented, not fixed.

The single failure policy charges allowance on uncertain failures at sites that used to refund. With production caps of 80 calls and 80k tokens per day and multi-step agents coming, the agent track must raise the caps deliberately (infra/main.bicep:43-49) and the UI should show remaining allowance.

Own-transaction settlement gives up atomicity between domain rows and usage rows: a crash between the provider reply and settle leaves a 'reserved' reservation. S11 housekeeping settles stale reservations at the estimate; until then they hold allowance.

Each paid request briefly uses two pooled connections; the pool is 5 + 5 with a 10 s timeout. Fine for one learner, but concurrent agent streams plus the job loop should be watched through the new metrics before raising pool_size.

`alembic check` may fail on day one because of existing ORM-versus-migration drift (JSONB defaults, server defaults, naming). It must be run locally and reconciled before it becomes a blocking CI step.

Test churn is real and deliberate in four places: 502 to 503 (test_turns.py, test_speech_api.py), usage after model failure (test_turns.py:190 and three other files), GET /today (about twelve calls in test_stories.py and the stories.spec.ts route regex), and the release-tool test for imperative env updates. Each is confined to one commit with the behaviour change.

Server-side prefetch bypasses Playwright page.route mocks. Extending it beyond /me requires the UX tracks to move Today, stories and videos specs from browser mocks to real fixture data; otherwise those specs silently test the wrong data.

ChatResult and ChatModel changes overlap with the ChatModel v2 track: tests build ChatResult positionally and monkeypatch complete/complete_once on provider instances. Field names (cumulative tokens), the new ProviderRejected class and the location of schema_instruction must be agreed once, or the two tracks will conflict.

Voice Live (P7) needs a browser WebSocket, but Next route handlers cannot upgrade and the API is internal-only. That track must add an upgrade handler in a small custom Node server in the web container (verifying Easy Auth and signing the assertion) or a second ingress; it also interacts with API sizing and the one-replica rule.
The jti replay cache and the job heartbeat both assume one API replica (or one worker). Scaling replicas needs a shared replay store and the optional worker app first.

Delivery changes touch production: the first declarative apply of infra/apps.bicep can revert imperative settings (public ingress, CURRICULUM_ADMIN_EMAILS, MAX_AUDIO_SECONDS); GHCR import needs a read credential and range-request support; storage lifecycle rules can delete learner evidence if prefixes are wrong. Each needs what-if output and an owner check before running.
Visual baselines must be generated on the CI Linux runner (the owner develops on Windows) and only after the P1 re-skin; otherwise they fail on font rendering or churn completely.

Prettier's one-off commit conflicts with every open branch; it has to be the first merge of the whole programme, and S15 deliberately leaves SkillTopicPractice and TopicConversation unsplit because P4 and P6 replace them.
