design.approach_summary:
Checked against Microsoft docs on 2026-10-05: Voice Live in West Europe offers only cascaded text models (Azure Speech STT → LLM → Azure TTS). That suits this product: transcription can be pinned to nl-BE, the Belgian voices work, function tools and per-response overrides exist, and token usage arrives per response. No scoped browser token is documented. WebRTC now exists, but on a preview api-version, globally routed, with transcripts delivered to the browser.

Recommendation: the API process is the session broker. It holds one outbound WebSocket to Voice Live (managed identity) behind a new stateful `RealtimeVoice` port. The browser leg uses the existing signed `/api` proxy: an SSE event stream down and sequenced PCM16 chunk POSTs up. This needs no new ingress, no CSP change and no custom Next server. The price is roughly 0.2–0.35 s extra latency (an estimate, measured in the spike); a ticketed relay container app is plan B.

Each learner turn is two bounded in-session passes. A forced tool call proposes an interpretation; code validates it against the server-received transcript using the partner's existing rules; then an anchored spoken reply runs under a contradiction guard with an authored fallback.

Sessions reserve new `voice_seconds` and `voice_tokens` allowances up front, are capped by the server clock, settled from measured usage, and reaped conservatively after a crash. Transcripts (no audio) are speaking evidence; points go through the activity service. Push-to-talk is the default, open mic is opt-in. Fixture and local-cascade adapters keep CI, e2e and laptop runs free.

Estimated cost is $0.08–0.20 per five-minute session, ±50%. Nothing here has been run against Azure yet; the spike gates the build.

key_decisions.decision: Azure facts the design rests on (verified 2026-10-05), including corrections to the brief
key_decisions.choice: West Europe Voice Live models: gpt-4o, 4o-mini, 4.1, 4.1-mini, 4.1-nano, 5.6-terra, 5.6-luna, 5, 5-mini, 5-nano on Data Zone Standard; gpt-5.4, 5.2, 5.1 on Global Standard. No gpt-realtime*, azure-realtime or phi4-mm-realtime. Tier follows model (Pro / Standard / Lite). STT: `input_audio_transcription {model:'azure-speech', language:'nl-BE'}`; the default multilingual model excludes Dutch, so the language must be explicit. Voices: any Azure TTS voice via `{type:'azure-standard', name:'nl-BE-DenaNeural'}`. Auth: Entra bearer (Cognitive Services User + Foundry User roles) or api-key. Limits: 60 min per connection, 100 new connections/min, 100–120k tokens/min. Billing: about 10 input and 20 output audio tokens per second. Function calling is supported; content filter cannot be disabled. Transcript events: `conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed` and `response.audio_transcript.delta/done`.
key_decisions.why: Sources: learn.microsoft.com speech-service pages voice-live (ms.date 2026-09-29), voice-live-how-to (2026-09-24), voice-live-webrtc (2026-09-29), regions?tabs=voice-live (2026-09-30), voice-live-language-support, speech-services-quotas-and-limits, voice-live-api-reference-2025-10-01; prices.azure.com retail API filtered to westeurope. Standard-tier meters per 1K tokens: speech audio in $0.015, out $0.026, text in $0.00066, cached $0.00033, out $0.00264.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Brief said WebSocket is server-to-server only. Docs now also describe a WebRTC endpoint (`/voice-live/realtime/calls`) and recommend it for client apps, but it uses api-version 2026-01-01-preview, 'global standard deployments' routed to the nearest region, and sends transcripts to the browser data channel. Inferred, not yet proven: nl-BE is accepted by Voice Live's azure-speech (docs say all STT locales); the existing SpeechServices-kind account suffices (docs say a Speech resource works but Foundry resources are 'optimized'). Semantic VAD and end-of-utterance models do not list Dutch.

key_decisions.decision: Transport between browser and Voice Live
key_decisions.choice: The API process brokers the session: one outbound `wss://<speech-custom-domain>/voice-live/realtime` connection per session. The browser leg uses the existing `/api` proxy: `GET /voice/sessions/{id}/events` (SSE down, base64 PCM16 24 kHz plus captions) and `POST /voice/sessions/{id}/audio?seq=n` (16 kHz PCM16 chunks of 160–400 ms, self-clocked, one request in flight).
key_decisions.why: Every request keeps the 60 s signed assertion and X-Requested-With. API ingress stays `external: false`; `connect-src 'self'` in apps/web/proxy.ts is unchanged; the standalone `node server.js` image is unchanged. The proxy already streams `upstream.body` and forwards content-type. ACA's 240 s limit is an idle timeout (default 4 min), so 10 s keep-alives should carry a 5-minute stream; the spike confirms this. Estimated extra latency is 0.2–0.35 s on a 1.3–1.8 s cascaded pipeline, acceptable for A1 learners if the spike confirms.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Browser-direct: no scoped ephemeral secret is documented for Voice Live; a raw Entra token or key in the browser bypasses reservations, caps and code validation and needs a CSP change. (b) WebSocket on the API with external ingress: breaks 'the API is never public'. (c) Custom Next server: Next 16.3 docs say standalone output and a custom server 'cannot be used together'; it would change the whole web image. (d) Dedicated relay app with a signed ticket: kept as plan B, see next decision. (e) WebRTC with a server-held control socket: best media path, but preview, globally routed, browser-reported transcripts, and hard to fake in CI. Revisit when GA in West Europe.

key_decisions.decision: Plan B if the latency exit criterion fails
key_decisions.choice: A relay container app `${name}-voice` running the same image with `python -m uvicorn dlp.voice_relay.app:app`: external ingress, WebSocket only, minReplicas 0 / maxReplicas 1, 0.25 vCPU / 0.5 Gi, own managed identity. It validates a single-use HS256 ticket (aud `dlp-voice`, 60 s, issued by `POST /voice/sessions` through the normal proxy) and checks Origin.
key_decisions.why: The port, director, runtime, tables and UI are transport-agnostic, so only the edge adapter (routes_voice stream handlers versus a WS handler) and the web uploader change.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Not chosen first because it adds a public surface holding database credentials, a second identity path, a new Key Vault secret (`voice-ticket-key`), a CSP revision (`connect-src wss://<relay-fqdn>` from env in apps/web/proxy.ts), a cold start, and a second process in dev and e2e. ACA rule-based routing could restore same-origin later but changes PUBLIC_ORIGIN and Easy Auth redirects.

key_decisions.decision: Runtime concurrency model inside the sync API
key_decisions.choice: Thread-based and synchronous. `websockets.sync.client` (websockets 16.1.1 is already in requirements-azure.lock via uvicorn[standard]); one reader thread per live session; SSE as a sync generator; audio POSTs as sync handlers writing to the provider socket. A process-wide registry allows at most 1 concurrent session.
key_decisions.why: Matches the all-sync codebase and its pytest setup (no pytest-asyncio). DB work stays in short `session_scope()` units, so no row lock or transaction is held across the session. Stream routes use `principal_dep` only, never `Depends(get_session)`.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: asyncio runtime on the uvicorn loop: first async domain code, a new test stack, and sync SQLAlchemy would need thread hops anyway. The `azure-ai-voicelive` SDK: async-only in the documented samples and a new hash-locked dependency; the adapter may adopt it later behind the port.

key_decisions.choice: VAD or push-to-talk commits the learner item with `create_response:false`. The runtime waits for the server-side transcript. Pass 1: `response.create` with text modality and forced `tool_choice` on `report_learner_turn`, whose parameters are the existing `TopicInterpretation` schema. Code runs `validate_meaning(step, transcript, proposed)` and advances the goal. Pass 2: a spoken reply with per-response instructions built from the code-chosen anchor. A guard scans `response.audio_transcript.delta`; on a trip it cancels, flushes playback and speaks the authored line.
key_decisions.why: Same interpret → validate → compose contract and tests as the typed partner. In cascaded mode the transcript is exactly what the LLM received, so substring grounding is exact. Only the validated tool path changes state; a leaked sentence is a UX flaw, not an integrity breach. Authored lines (hint, cue, fallback, closing) are synthesised through the existing `TextToSpeech` port so wording is exact.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Single pass with async function calling: faster, but the partner may announce progress code has not accepted. Kept as the fallback if two-pass p50 exceeds 2.0 s. Separate `ChatModel.complete_once` interpretation per turn: same latency, extra billing path. Post-conversation interpretation only: goals could not drive the dialogue.

key_decisions.choice: Standard-tier EU Data Zone text model chosen by spike latency (candidates gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5-mini, gpt-4.1-mini). `azure-speech` with single language `nl-BE` and a `phrase_list` from scenario names and aliases. Voice `nl-BE-DenaNeural` (Arnaud selectable), `rate` 0.85–1.0 by stage. Input pcm16 16 kHz, output pcm16 24 kHz. `azure_deep_noise_suppression` and `server_echo_cancellation`. api-version 2026-04-10.
key_decisions.why: Keeps EU processing (GO_LIVE: do not silently select Global) and Belgian Standard Dutch. Models are fully managed by Voice Live, so no Bicep model deployment. A config validator refuses the three Global-only models unless explicitly overridden.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: gpt-realtime family: not deployable in West Europe, OpenAI voices, Dutch only at the WER<50% bar. Sweden Central resource: moves data and adds a resource for no Belgian-voice gain. MAI Transcribe: preview, generic `nl`. HD/Dragon voices: no nl-BE voice. Pronunciation assessment: excluded by owner decision.

key_decisions.choice: Push-to-talk (hold or tap-to-finish, `turn_detection: null`, explicit commit) is the default at every level. Open mic (`server_vad`, silence 900 ms, `interrupt_response` and `auto_truncate` true) is an opt-in with a headphones hint.
key_decisions.why: Semantic VAD and end-of-utterance models do not list Dutch, and learners pause mid-sentence. Half-duplex removes loudspeaker echo on phones, reduces streamed input seconds, and reuses `talkButtonHandlers` from apps/web/lib/client/recorder.ts.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Open mic by default: premature turn ends for beginners, echo false triggers on phone speakers, higher cost.

key_decisions.choice: New metrics `voice_seconds` and `voice_tokens` in `usage.METRICS` and `limits_for`. `POST /voice/sessions` reserves max_seconds (300) and a token ceiling before any provider connection. The server clock enforces 300 s per session, 16 learner turns, a 60 s connect window, an idle limit and a token ceiling. Close commits measured connected seconds and summed `response.done.usage`. Never connected → release. Crash or deploy → reaper commits `last_seen_at - connected_at + 15 s`, or the full reservation if unknown. No automatic reconnect or replay to Azure.
key_decisions.why: Keeps reserve → call → settle and 'uncertain paid calls are never silently replayed'. Separate metrics stop a session from starving the 60 s clip allowance (1200 audio seconds/day) or the 80k/day chat token cap, since most voice tokens are cheap cached text.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Reusing `audio_seconds` and `tokens`: one session would consume about 25% and 40% of the daily caps and distort chat budgeting. Settling only from client reports: untrusted.

key_decisions.choice: Both transcripts are appended to the partner conversation (mode `live`, `input_mode: live_voice`) as turns complete. Learner audio is not stored. On end: `record_observation(skill='speaking')`, with `assessed` true only for non-fixture providers; `record_activity(kind='live_conversation')` with effort points per spoken turn (proposed 2 per turn, cap 10 per session, final values owned by the P3 points table); P6 post-conversation feedback runs over the transcript.
key_decisions.why: Audio reaches the server and is transcribed server-side, so it is genuine speaking practice (D-16). Voice routes accept PCM only, never a client transcript. No pronunciation or accent field exists anywhere (D-20). A 5-minute PCM capture is 10–14 MB, which is privacy and cost without a current use.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Storing recordings in Blob as AudioAsset: deferred until a replay feature needs it. A separate `voice_turns` table: would duplicate the partner history and drift.

key_decisions.choice: `RealtimeVoice.open(config) -> RealtimeVoiceSession` in providers/base.py, with `send_audio`, `commit_turn`, `request_reply`, `send_tool_result`, `add_assistant_text`, `cancel_reply`, `next_event(timeout)`, `close() -> VoiceUsage`. Adapters: `AzureVoiceLive` (providers/voice_azure.py), `LocalCascadeVoice` (providers/voice_local.py, composes the existing STT, ChatModel and TTS ports, push-to-talk only), `FixtureRealtimeVoice` (providers/fixtures.py).
key_decisions.why: Domain code depends only on the port. The fixture replays apps/api/tests/fixtures/voice_script.json on a byte-count clock (no wall clock), emits transcript, tool call, reply text, tone audio and usage, and supports failure injection (drop mid-session, transcription failed, invalid tool JSON). The cascade adapter runs in CI over fixture ports and on the laptop over Ollama, faster-whisper and Piper.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Letting the domain speak Realtime events directly: vendor leakage and no fake. Callback-style port: harder to test than a pull-based `next_event`.

key_decisions.choice: Captions come from server-forwarded transcripts: partner text per sentence after the guard, learner text after transcription. Gloss for generated partner lines is an on-demand or auto (beginner gloss levels) translation via LlmGateway, cached on the turn and labelled automatic. Authored lines reuse authored en/fa text.
key_decisions.why: Generated replies have no authored translations. An in-session translation response would pollute the conversation context, and `conversation:'none'` is unverified on Voice Live. Persian renders through `<LearningText>` with lang=fa dir=rtl.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Translating every caption eagerly at all levels: unnecessary cost above beginner levels. No gloss: contradicts the bilingual-beginner decision.

key_decisions.choice: The in-process session registry requires the API to stay at maxReplicas 1, asserted at startup when voice is enabled. Flag `VOICE_LIVE_ENABLED` (default false) plus `VOICE_PROVIDER` off|fixture|local|azure. Production accepts azure or off only, and voice also needs PAID_USAGE_ENABLED. API sizing stays 0.25 vCPU / 0.5 Gi unless the spike shows more than 50 ms p95 thread lag; then `apiCpu` 0.5 / `apiMemory` 1Gi, which roughly doubles the API compute line.
key_decisions.why: One learner means one session. Audio relay is a few percent of a core. A revision rollout ends a live session, and the lifespan shutdown hook settles it. The web app keeps minReplicas 0 because a live session generates continuous requests.
key_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Redis or database-backed session fan-out: unjustified for one replica. Always-on relay replica: fixed cost for an occasional feature.

steps.title: Turn director, prompts and reply guard (pure code)
steps.what: director.py is a deterministic state machine: VoiceEvent in, commands and client events out. Two bounded passes per learner turn (forced report_learner_turn, then anchored reply). Goal decisions use TopicInterpretation and validate_meaning. It guards reply deltas (no closing before completion, no unaccepted facts) with authored fallback, and handles hint/repeat, the T-30 s wrap-up, turn and token ceilings, and transcription-failed re-asks. prompts.py builds the session config: nl-BE pin, voice, rate by stage, phrase hints, untrusted-speech rules.

Routes: GET …/events (SSE, keep-alive 10 s, resume with ?after=, Cache-Control no-store no-transform), POST …/audio (octet-stream ≤64 KB, monotonic seq, duplicates dropped), POST …/control (commit, interrupt, hint, repeat, ping). principal_dep only; DB in session_scope units.

api.response: {enabled: bool, provider_label: 'azure-neural'|'synthetic-development'|'fixture', voice: str, locale: 'nl-BE', max_session_seconds: int, turn_modes: ['push','open'], open_mic_allowed: bool, remaining_seconds_today: number, sample_rate_in: 16000, sample_rate_out: 24000}
api.notes: No provider call, no writes. `enabled` is false when the flag is off, the provider is 'off', or (azure) paid usage is not approved. The web hides the Live mode when false.

api.response: 201/200 {id, status:'reserved', conversation_id, scenario:{title, role, setup, opening, goals}, turn_mode, max_seconds, connect_expires_at, voice, label, review_status:'unreviewed', stream:{events_path, audio_path, control_path, chunk_ms_min:160, chunk_ms_max:400}}
api.notes: This is the ticket step: the grant is the server-side reserved row with a 60 s connect window, not a bearer credential. Idempotent on request_id (409 if reused with a different payload). Reserves voice_seconds and voice_tokens before any provider connection. Errors: 403 paid usage not enabled, 409 a session is already active, 429 allowance or daily start cap, 503 provider unavailable. Under plan B it also returns {ticket, relay_url}.

api.response: {id, status, end_reason, turn_mode, seconds_used, seconds_left, turns:[{seq, speaker, text, gloss?, accepted?, assisted, reply_source?}], goals:[{goal, met, assisted}], summary, points_awarded, feedback_status}
api.notes: Owner-scoped (404 otherwise). Runs lazy reap_stale. Never returns interpretation proposals, aliases or required_groups.

api.response: SSE events with ids = seq: ready, state{goals, seconds_left}, speech_started (flush playback), learner_caption{seq, text}, partner_caption_delta / partner_caption{seq, text, reply_source}, audio{seq, sample_rate, pcm16_b64}, goal{id, met}, warning{seconds_left}, ended{reason, summary_path}. Comment keep-alive every 10 s. Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform.
api.notes: The first successful call inside the connect window opens the provider session and starts the clock. A reconnect resumes from `after` (captions and state replayed, audio older than 2 s dropped). Uses principal_dep only and holds no DB session. 409 if not reserved or live, 410 if ended. Does not rely on Last-Event-ID, which the proxy drops today.

api.request: Content-Type: application/octet-stream; body = PCM16 LE mono 16 kHz, 160 ms to 2 s (≤ 64 KB); X-Requested-With: fetch
api.response: 200 {ack: n, seconds_left}
api.notes: seq is strictly increasing. Duplicates are acknowledged and dropped (idempotent retry); gaps are tolerated and counted. 409 before the event stream is connected, 410 after end, 413 oversize, 422 odd byte length. Accepts audio only; there is no transcript field anywhere.

api.response: 200 {accepted: bool, seconds_left}
api.notes: commit ends a push-to-talk turn. interrupt cancels the current reply. hint and repeat speak the authored line and mark the goal assisted. ping keeps liveness in push mode. Idempotent on client_event_id.

api.response: Same shape as GET /voice/sessions/{id}
api.notes: Idempotent. Closes the provider session, settles both reservations from measured usage, finishes the conversation, and records the observation, activity and feedback request.

api.response: {seq, gloss:{en?|fa?}, source: 'authored'|'automatic'}
api.notes: Partner turns only. Cached on the turn. An automatic gloss is one LlmGateway call reserved against the chat allowances (429 when exhausted, with no call). An authored line makes no call.

api.response: counters gains voice_seconds and voice_tokens, each with daily and total {used, reserved, limit, remaining}
api.notes: UsagePanel shows the two new rows. estimated_cost includes voice once pricing_entries are seeded.

Crash drill (dev, fixture provider with a slow script): kill the API mid-session. After restart, GET /voice/sessions/{id} shows status interrupted, both reservations committed (not released), turns persisted up to the crash, no points double-awarded, and a new session can start.

Owner live check after P7.12 (paid, flag enabled for the owner only): `python scripts/verify_live.py --voice` runs one scripted session; then one real five-minute conversation on a laptop and one on a phone. Next day, compare /usage voice_seconds and voice_tokens with the Speech resource cost line (target within ±25%); preflight shows 'live voice … last live use'.

COST ESTIMATE per five-minute session, West Europe retail USD on 2026-10-05, Standard tier. Push-to-talk, 12 turns: learner audio ~90 s ≈ 900 tokens ≈ $0.014; partner speech ~100 s ≈ 2,000 tokens ≈ $0.052; text ~29K input (about half cached) plus ~1.4K output ≈ $0.02; total ≈ $0.085. Open mic with silence billed: ≈ $0.12–0.15. Pro-tier model: ≈ $0.20–0.30. Uncertainty ±50%: silence billing, cached-history accounting, real tokens per second, and two-pass text overhead are unmeasured.

Cost in context: the recorded-turn flow costs roughly $0.05 for the same speech, based on recalled list prices (STT $1 per audio hour, neural TTS $15 per 1M characters). The default cap of 600 voice seconds per day bounds spend at about $0.40 per day, against the 50-unit monthly budget alert.

Critical files for implementation: apps/api/src/dlp/providers/base.py; apps/api/src/dlp/providers/registry.py; apps/api/src/dlp/domains/usage/service.py; apps/api/src/dlp/domains/topic_conversations/workflow.py; apps/web/app/api/[...path]/route.ts; infra/main.bicep (all under the worktree root named in `track`).
open_risks: Dutch recognition quality for hesitant, accented A1 speech through Voice Live's azure-speech path is unmeasured. It is the single most likely reason for a no-go (S2). Mitigation: phrase_list from scenario vocabulary, single-language pin, and the recorded-turn flow as a permanent fallback.

Whether nl-BE (rather than only nl-NL) is accepted by Voice Live's `language` field is inferred from 'all Speech-to-text locales are supported' and not shown in a Voice Live example. Likewise, whether the existing SpeechServices-kind account suffices or a Foundry (AIServices) account is needed is unproven. Either outcome changes Bicep but not the design.

Latency budget: cascaded STT → LLM → TTS, plus the two-pass grounding, plus the HTTP-duplex leg may land near 2 s from end of speech to first audio. Reasoning-class GPT-5 models may be slower than gpt-4.1-mini, which is deprecated and retires 2027-04-14. The spike decides model and one-pass versus two-pass. Plan B (relay) removes only about 0.25 s.

The HTTP-duplex leg is unconventional: about 3–6 small POSTs per second through Easy Auth, Next and the API, plus one long SSE response. Risks are Next response compression buffering the stream, the BaseHTTPMiddleware in main.py masking disconnects, undici or ACA idle timers, and request-metric noise. All are checked in S8; the ticketed relay app is the fallback.

Turn detection is not Dutch-aware (semantic VAD, filler-word removal and end-of-utterance models list ten languages without Dutch). Open mic may cut learners off mid-thought or wait too long, hence push-to-talk by default. Open mic may remain permanently opt-in.

The contradiction guard acts on streamed text while audio is already flowing, so a few syllables of a rejected reply can be heard before the authored fallback. State integrity is unaffected because only the validated tool path changes state.

Voice Live's built-in content filter cannot be tuned or disabled, and its classifiers are not trained on Dutch. False blocks or odd refusals in harmless scenarios are possible. The runtime maps them to an authored re-ask and counts them.

Usage counters are application estimates. Voice Live bills by tokens, with rates only approximately 10 and 20 per second. Silence billing in open mic and cached-history accounting are unknown until S6. Several retail meters changed in 2026-05 and 2026-10, so prices are kept as dated data.

A process crash between provider activity and the next 15 s heartbeat leaves up to about 15–30 s of uncertain usage. The reaper charges conservatively, so the learner may lose a little allowance, never the reverse. A revision rollout ends any live session.

Single-replica coupling: the in-process registry means the API can never scale out while voice is enabled without moving to plan B or shared state. The 0.25 vCPU replica also runs the job loop; GIL contention during a story or video job could cause audible jitter (measured in S8; bump to 0.5 vCPU if needed).

Mobile Safari: AudioContext must start from a user gesture; the play-and-record audio session lowers and reroutes output; backgrounding or locking suspends capture; Bluetooth headsets switch to 16 kHz HFP. Each needs device testing that fixtures cannot provide. The Dockerfile currently copies no public/ directory, so worklets would 404 in production without the P7.9 fix and its CI check.

Cross-track assumptions: this plan presumes P6 exposes a conversation row that accepts mode 'live' and pure decide / anchor / guard functions; P5 supplies an SSE helper, proxy abort forwarding and LlmGateway; P3 supplies record_activity; P2 supplies the profile and copy catalogue. If names differ, P7.3, P7.4, P7.8 and P7.10 adapt, but the port, runtime and transport do not.

WebRTC is the better long-term media path (UDP, native echo cancellation, no audio through our tiers). Today it is preview, globally routed, and puts transcripts on the browser channel. The port and director are designed so a later switch replaces only the edge transport; that switch would need a new decision entry and a way to fake a WebRTC peer in CI.

Data volume is roughly 10–16 MB per five-minute session (PCM16 with base64 on the downlink). The Save-Data path uses 16 kHz output or the recorded-turn flow, but the feature is inherently heavier than the existing Opus upload path.
